issues.title: GTK apps (e.g. Nautilus) freeze on close under Hyprland/NVIDIA unless forcing GSK_RENDERER=ngl
issues.body:
**Summary**

Hit an issue where Nautilus froze every time I closed the window. To debug:

- Ran Nautilus from terminal with GDK_BACKEND=wayland to watch logs
- Tailed journalctl --user -f and dmesg -w — no OOM/segfaults, just a hang
- Verified that GDK_BACKEND=x11 closed cleanly → narrowed to Wayland path
- Tried GTK_USE_PORTAL=0 alone and it still froze
- Forced GSK_RENDERER=gl, it closed cleanly, but showed a deprecated warning
- Finally used GSK_RENDERER=ngl, works, closes fine

So it’s GTK4’s Vulkan renderer hanging on teardown (NVIDIA Quadro M1200 here, but likely all NVIDIA).

FYI I also confirmed the calculator hangs as well. 

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Run Nautilus under Wayland:

```bash
GDK_BACKEND=wayland nautilus --no-desktop
```

2. Close the window
3. Observe freeze (no crash, just hang)

**Workaround**

Run the app with ngl renderer instead of Vulkan:

`GDK_BACKEND=wayland GTK_USE_PORTAL=0 GSK_RENDERER=ngl nautilus --no-desktop`

**Permanent local fixes**

a) App-specific (minimal):

Patch the desktop entry so Nautilus always runs with ngl:

```bash
# In case it doesn’t already exist
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/applications
cp /usr/share/applications/org.gnome.Nautilus.desktop ~/.local/share/applications/

# Then edit ~/.local/share/applications/org.gnome.Nautilus.desktop
# Change this line:
# Exec=nautilus --new-window %U

# To this:
Exec=env GSK_RENDERER=ngl nautilus --new-window %U
```

b) Global (affects all GTK4 apps):

Add to Hyprland envs:

```bash
# ~/.config/hypr/envs.conf
env = GSK_RENDERER,ngl
```

issues.title: Browser crash, probably from video autoplay, freezes Hyprland
issues.body:
# Chromium/Brave SIGILL on video playback (NVIDIA) crashes Hyprland — hard reboot required

## System

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Arch Linux |
| Kernel | 7.0.9-arch2-1 |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 9 5900X |
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 |
| NVIDIA driver | nvidia-open-dkms 595.71.05-2 |
| libva-nvidia-driver | 0.0.17-1 |
| Chromium | 148.0.7778.178-1 |
| Brave | 1.92.108 beta |
| Hyprland | 0.55.2-1 |
| Omarchy | (current as of 2026-05-30 upgrade) |


## What happened

Playing video on social/commerce sites (confirmed: Facebook, Twitter, Amazon)
often causes Chromium or Brave to crash and Hyprland to freeze unrecoverably. I'm still
able to shell into the system but as for the physical console I can't even switch
to a different VT.

## Investigation

I shelled in to the system and asked Claude to attempt recovery and
investigate the cause. I rejected some implausible conclusions and now
present one which seems plausible to me (fwiw!).

The browser crashes with SIGILL in its internal Media decoder
thread. The crash leaves an NVDEC hardware decode session open without freeing
it. The NVIDIA GSP firmware then times out waiting for a cleanup RPC, enters
a faulted state, and Hyprland loses its GPU context and aborts. Hyprland's
watchdog restarts it in safe mode, but safe mode fails to bind its socket.
With Wayland mediating VT switching, there is no escape to a TTY.

This happened twice in one day: once with stock Chromium (Facebook),
once with Brave beta (Amazon), each time requiring a reboot.
I've already tried the "ignore the problem; maybe it will go away" solution
but am now filing this issue—it's hard to see how it could be affecting
only me.

## Relationship to existing issues

This is distinct from #2964 (AMD GPU ring timeout during Google Meet) and
#3891 (ANGLE/EGL video rendering broken after Mesa update). Those are GPU
rendering pipeline failures on AMD hardware. This is a crash in Chromium's
software-side media decode thread on NVIDIA hardware, which then wedges the
GPU driver.

The surface symptom — Chromium takes down Hyprland, reboot required — is the
same, but the root cause and affected hardware are different.

## Workaround (unconfirmed)

Add `--disable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder` to
`~/.config/chromium-flags.conf`. This disables only hardware video
decode (NVDEC via VA-API); GPU rasterization, compositing, WebGL, and
canvas acceleration are unaffected.

## Further unconfirmed analysis from Claude

This is Claude writing now:

### Hyprland

When Hyprland crashes (SIGABRT, triggered by GPU context loss after an NVIDIA
driver fault), its watchdog restarts it in safe mode. The safe mode instance
fails to bind its socket, producing a non-functional compositor. Because VT
switching on Wayland is compositor-mediated rather than kernel-handled, the
user has no means of escaping to a TTY. The only recovery is a hard power-off.

There are two bugs here:
1. Safe mode instance fails to bind its socket
2. A broken compositor fully blocks VT switching with no kernel-level escape hatch

### Chromium

Chromium's Media thread terminates with SIGILL (illegal instruction) when playing
video on high-media sites (confirmed: Facebook, Amazon; also reproduced with Brave
1.92.108 beta on Twitter). The crash is deterministic — the same code address is hit
on every occurrence. The process dies without releasing its NVDEC/VA-API resources,
which cascades into an NVIDIA GSP firmware timeout (Xid 175) that degrades the GPU
driver state, takes down the Hyprland compositor, and leaves the system in an
unrecoverable state requiring a hard reboot.

#### Crash detail

##### Kernel trap message (boot of 2026-05-30, Chromium 148.0.7778.96-1)

```
07:27:14  kernel: traps: Media[320806] trap invalid opcode
          ip:55a64c04e477 sp:7f39907fbf50 error:0
          in chromium[8d62477,55a644848000+10240000]
07:27:14  systemd-coredump: Process 320640 (chromium) of user 1000
          terminated abnormally with signal 4/ILL
```

The crashing process is a `--type=renderer` subprocess. The thread named "Media"
is Chromium's in-process media decoder thread. The crash address is identical across
multiple occurrences (different sessions, different browser versions), pointing to a
deterministic code path rather than memory corruption.

The same pattern reproduces with Brave 1.92.108 beta (same upstream Chromium media
pipeline):

```
15:37:55  traps: Media[38436] trap invalid opcode ip:5561296141e8 in brave[...]
15:41:59  traps: Media[41157] trap invalid opcode ip:5561296141e8  ← same address
15:42:28  traps: Media[41963] trap invalid opcode ip:5561296141e8  ← same address
```

##### Coredump summary

```
Signal:   4 (ILL)
Process:  chromium --type=renderer [...]
Thread:   "Media" (worker thread, not main)
Storage:  truncated core (symbols stripped in release build)
Stack:    #0  0x000055a64c04e477 n/a (n/a + 0x0)
```

The binary contains a large number of `ud2` sequences (478,277 in the current
build), consistent with `CHECK()`/`IMMEDIATE_CRASH()` usage throughout the codebase.
The most likely explanation is an assertion failure in the media decode pipeline —
possibly in the VA-API/NVDEC interaction path — rather than a CPU ISA incompatibility.


#### Cascade

After the renderer process dies with SIGILL, the NVIDIA GSP firmware times out
waiting for a `FREE` RPC that will never arrive (the client is dead):

```
07:28:43  kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0b:00): 175, pid=69435, name=chromium,
          Timeout after 75s of waiting for RPC response from GPU0 GSP!
          Expected function 10 (FREE) sequence 230682 (0xbeef0403 0x0).
07:28:46  kernel: NVRM: GPU0 _kgspLogGspTraceCrashBuffer: [dump follows]
```

This leaves the NVIDIA driver in a degraded state. When a subsequent Chromium/Brave
crash occurs (or as a delayed consequence), Hyprland loses its GPU context and
aborts:

```
15:47:30  Hyprland (PID 1852): SIGABRT
15:47:30  xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland (PID 2185): SIGSEGV
```

Hyprland's watchdog restarts it in safe mode, but safe mode fails to bind its
socket. Under Wayland, VT switching is compositor-mediated; with a non-functional
compositor, keyboard VT switching is completely unavailable. Hard reboot required.

issues.title: Quattro upgrade drops non-US keyboard layout when vconsole.conf only has KEYMAP
issues.body:
### System details

- Omarchy 4.0.0-1 (Quattro stable), upgraded from a pre-Quattro installation
- Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3
- Intel Core Ultra 5 228V
- Intel Arc Graphics 130V/140V
- French/AZERTY keyboard layout

### What's wrong?

After upgrading an existing Omarchy installation to Quattro and rebooting, the Hyprland session uses the US/QWERTY layout instead of the previously configured French/AZERTY layout.

Before the upgrade, the active legacy config contained:

```conf
# ~/.config/hypr/input.conf
input {
  kb_layout = fr
  kb_options = compose:caps
}
```

The system console config contains:

```conf
# /etc/vconsole.conf
KEYMAP=fr
```

It does not contain `XKBLAYOUT`, which is valid: `vconsole.conf` only guarantees the console `KEYMAP` setting.

The Quattro upgrade leaves the legacy `input.conf` in place but switches Hyprland to the new Lua entry points. It always installs a stock `~/.config/hypr/input.lua`, and that file has no active keyboard-layout override. The packaged `default/hypr/input.lua` then does:

```lua
local kb_layout = vconsole.XKBLAYOUT or "us"
```

Because this installation has `KEYMAP=fr` but no `XKBLAYOUT`, the effective layout silently falls back to `us`. The migration `1781485962.sh` also sees the stock `input.lua` and leaves/replaces it with the packaged version, so the old `kb_layout = fr` is never carried over.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a pre-Quattro Omarchy installation where:
   - `~/.config/hypr/input.conf` contains `kb_layout = fr`
   - `/etc/vconsole.conf` contains only `KEYMAP=fr`
2. Upgrade to Quattro.
3. Reboot into the new Lua-based Hyprland configuration.
4. Type in any application.
5. Observe that the session uses US/QWERTY instead of French/AZERTY.

#### Expected behavior

The Quattro upgrade should preserve the explicitly configured keyboard layout from the legacy `input.conf`.

#### Actual behavior

The explicit legacy layout is ignored, and the new default falls back to `us`.

#### Workaround

Adding this to `~/.config/hypr/input.lua` restores the correct layout:

```lua
hl.config({
  input = {
    kb_layout = "fr",
  },
})
```

#### Suggested fix

During `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`, migrate active `kb_layout`, `kb_variant`, and `kb_options` values from the legacy `~/.config/hypr/input.conf` into the new `input.lua` before switching entry points. Alternatively, ensure the upgrade populates an appropriate `XKBLAYOUT` when only `KEYMAP` exists, while accounting for console/XKB naming differences.

A regression test could cover a legacy `input.conf` with `kb_layout = fr` plus a `vconsole.conf` containing only `KEYMAP=fr`.

issues.title: Quattro Brave Origin stable migration strands the existing Beta browser profile
issues.body:
### System details

- Omarchy 4.0.0-1 (Quattro stable), upgraded from a pre-Quattro installation
- Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3
- Intel Core Ultra 5 228V
- Intel Arc Graphics 130V/140V
- Brave Origin Beta before upgrade: `brave-origin-beta-bin 1.94.109-1`
- Brave Origin stable after upgrade: `brave-origin-bin 1:1.93.136-1`

### What's wrong?

The Quattro migration `1784510887.sh` automatically installs Brave Origin stable, removes Brave Origin Beta, and changes the default browser:

```bash
omarchy-pkg-aur-add brave-origin-bin
omarchy-pkg-drop brave-origin-beta-bin
```

However, Beta and stable use different user-data directories:

- Beta: `~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Origin-Beta`
- Stable: `~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Origin`

The migration does not transfer or otherwise reconnect the existing profile. On first launch, stable creates a fresh profile, making the user's extensions, cookies/login sessions, history, and other browser state appear to have been deleted.

The data was not actually erased on this machine; it was stranded in the old Beta profile after the Beta package and launcher were removed.

#### Evidence from this installation

Pacman recorded the automatic switch at 20:31:

```text
installed brave-origin-bin (1:1.93.136-1)
removed brave-origin-beta-bin (1.94.109-1)
```

The old Beta profile was last modified immediately before the upgrade, while the new stable profile was created on the first post-upgrade launch:

```text
Brave-Origin-Beta: created 2026-07-08 23:25, last modified 2026-08-14 20:28
Brave-Origin:      created 2026-08-14 20:42
```

Without reading any browsing data, file metadata shows the profile discontinuity:

| Profile | Total size | History database | Cookies database | User extension directories |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Brave-Origin-Beta` | 5.2 GB | 7,274,496 bytes | 589,824 bytes | 4 |
| `Brave-Origin` | 82 MB | 163,840 bytes | 20,480 bytes | 0 |

This matches the observed behavior: Brave opens as a new browser with extensions gone, sites logged out, and history missing.

There is an additional downgrade risk: the migration replaced Beta 1.94.109 with stable 1.93.136, so blindly copying or reusing the newer Beta profile in the older stable build may be unsafe.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. On a pre-Quattro installation, use `brave-origin-beta-bin` as the default browser.
2. Accumulate history, cookies/login sessions, and install user extensions.
3. Upgrade to Quattro so migration `1784510887.sh` runs.
4. Launch the new default `brave-origin.desktop`.
5. Observe a fresh browser profile with the previous extensions, sessions, and history missing.
6. Compare `~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Origin-Beta` and `~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Origin`; the original data remains only in the Beta directory.

#### Expected behavior

A distribution upgrade should not make an existing browser profile disappear from the user's browser. The migration should preserve access to the existing profile or require an explicit, well-explained opt-in before switching release channels.

#### Actual behavior

The Beta package is removed and the default browser is changed to stable, which starts with a separate empty profile.

#### Suggested fix

Avoid automatically removing Brave Origin Beta during the Quattro upgrade. Keep it installed and selected until the user explicitly chooses to migrate to stable.

If an automatic migration is retained:

1. Back up the existing profile.
2. Ensure the target stable browser version is not older than the source Beta version.
3. Perform a supported profile migration from `Brave-Origin-Beta` to `Brave-Origin`.
4. Verify that extensions, cookies/session state, history, bookmarks, and saved credentials remain accessible before removing Beta.
5. Show a clear warning and recovery instructions if a safe migration cannot be guaranteed.

A regression test should create a populated Beta profile marker, run the migration, and verify that the replacement browser still uses or safely migrates that profile.

issues.title: omarchy-menu-keybindings hangs forever when a user Lua config iterates hl.get_monitors()
issues.body:
### What happened

`omarchy-menu-keybindings` (SUPER + K) never opens. The process hangs indefinitely — no menu, no error, no timeout. `omarchy-menu-keybindings --print` also hangs.

The hang is triggered by any user Lua config that iterates one of Hyprland's list getters (`hl.get_monitors()`, `hl.get_windows()`, `hl.get_workspaces()`) with `ipairs` at config-evaluation time.

### What I expected

The keybindings menu opens and lists the bindings, or fails loudly.

### Steps to reproduce

On Omarchy 4.0.0 (quattro), add a single line to `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua`:

```lua
for _, monitor in ipairs(hl.get_monitors()) do end
```

Then run:

```bash
omarchy-menu-keybindings --print   # hangs forever
```

Hyprland itself is fine — `hyprctl reload` and `hyprctl configerrors` are clean, and the config behaves correctly at runtime. Only the keybindings scanner hangs.

### Root cause

`build_lua_bind_cache()` in `omarchy-menu-keybindings` re-evaluates `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` in a bare `lua` interpreter, with `hl` replaced by a catch-all stub (bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings, around lines 181-232):

```lua
local noop
noop = setmetatable({}, {
  __index = function() return noop end,
  __call  = function() return noop end,
})
```

Because `__index` answers **every** key with a truthy value, `hl.get_monitors()` returns `noop`, and `ipairs(noop)` reads index 1, 2, 3, … without ever hitting `nil`. Infinite loop inside the `lua` subprocess. The `while read` loop feeding off it in bash blocks forever, so the menu never renders.

The stub already special-cases one getter to return a real value:

```lua
get_config = function()
  return nil
end,
```

The list getters just were not covered.

### Suggested fix

Stub the list getters with real empty tables, so iteration terminates:

```lua
get_monitors   = function() return {} end,
get_windows    = function() return {} end,
get_workspaces = function() return {} end,
```

A timeout around the `lua` subprocess would also turn this class of failure into a degraded menu instead of a silent hang.

### Why this probably was not caught

No config under `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/` calls any `hl.get_*` getter at load time (`grep -rn "get_monitors\|get_windows\|get_workspaces" /usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/` returns nothing), so the stock configs never hit it.

Third-party Lua modules do. Unmodified upstream [shezdy/hyprsplit](https://github.com/shezdy/hyprsplit) `init.lua` iterates all three getters, so any user requiring it from their Hypr config gets the same hang.

My own trigger was dynamic monitor placement — computing the laptop's position from the live external monitor geometry, rather than hardcoding `auto-right`.

### Workaround

Guard in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, right after the bootstrap `dofile`, detecting the stub (raw slot empty but `__index` conjures a value) and handing back real empty lists:

```lua
local probe = hl.get_monitors()
if type(probe) == "table" and rawget(probe, 1) == nil and probe[1] ~= nil then
  hl.get_monitors = function() return {} end
  hl.get_windows = function() return {} end
  hl.get_workspaces = function() return {} end
end
```

With that in place `omarchy-menu-keybindings --print` exits 0 and lists all 231 bindings.

### System details

- Omarchy 4.0.0-1 (stable channel)
- Hyprland 0.56.2-1
- Lua 5.5.1-1
- CPU: AMD Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 w/ Radeon 860M
- GPU: AMD Radeon 840M / 860M Graphics (Krackan)

issues.title: Post-update restart compiles new QML on the UI thread; bar and menus are dead until that finishes, and a second restart can lose the process
issues.body:
### System details

Intel Core i7-4790 / NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970 (`nvidia-580xx` 580.178.04), Samsung LC49G95T 3840×1080, Hyprland 0.56.2, Omarchy `4.0.0.r1761.g7be59e1-1` (channel: edge, package: `omarchy-dev`), kernel `7.1.8-arch1-3`, `quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7-1`, `qt6-base 6.11.1`

Related: #6748 (same update replaces `/usr/share/omarchy` under a live shell). The QML hot-reload / `FATAL: QPixmap` path is fixed. This is what is left.

### What's wrong?

After `omarchy-update`, the top bar is gone and Super/menus do nothing. `omarchy restart shell` can flash the bar and then leave none. A second restart brings bar and menus back.

This is not a crash (no coredump, no signal, no OOM) and it is not “updates randomly kill the shell.” The update’s own restart starts a new Quickshell that answers IPC immediately, then spends tens of seconds compiling the just-replaced QML on the UI thread. Until that compile finishes there is no bar and no menus. If you restart again during that window, kill and launch race and you are left with no shell at all.

### Root cause

`ensureService()` loads every first-party service with `Qt.createComponent(url, Component.PreferSynchronous)` (`shell.qml`). That compile runs on the Qt main thread.

`omarchy-update` writes a new `/usr/share/omarchy/shell` (this run: 114MB `omarchy-dev` replace), then `omarchy-update-restart` always calls `omarchy-restart-shell`. The new process must rebuild `~/.cache/quickshell/qmlcache` for the new sources.

`omarchy-restart-shell` treats the shell as up as soon as `omarchy-shell shell ping` works. Ping succeeds at `Configuration Loaded` — `shell.qml` is parsed, IPC is up — **before** the PreferSynchronous service compile has finished. The update even prints “Restarting shell / All plugins have been reloaded” *before* it calls restart, and swallows failure with `|| true`.

On this machine the cold compile took ~60s (73 cache files written at ~1/s from 09:25:48.98 to 09:27:00). AT-SPI logged `Disabling unresponsive app with pid 8094` at 09:26:05, in the middle of those writes. The qslog for that process does the same work as a fast start (same desktop-entry scan, same imports, same `j/status`); only the duration changes:

| Start | When | Config → `service-ready` | qmlcache |
|---|---|---|---|
| pid 1957 | login, old tree | ~7s | warm from previous days |
| pid 8094 | update restart, new tree | **60s** | 73 files written during the gap |
| pid 9634 | second manual restart | ~300ms | warm from 8094 |

So this does **not** happen on every update for everyone. It happens when the package replace invalidates enough qmlcache that a full rebuild is needed, and the CPU is slow enough (here: Haswell i7-4790, Chromium also just launched) that the rebuild outlasts the 2s ping window and the user’s patience. On a fast machine the same path can finish before anyone notices.

The second disappearance is a separate, smaller bug in the same script. `omarchy-restart-shell` claims `quickshell kill` waits for exit (“Requires our quickshell-git build; 0.3.0's kill returns immediately”). This box is `quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7-1`. At 09:27:00, during the still-running compile:

```
omarchy-shell[9194]: An instance of this configuration is already running.
omarchy-shell[8094]: Exiting due to IPC request.
```

Ping then fails (`20 × 0.1s`). No shell until the next restart.

Leftover from #6748, not what hid the bar: at 09:24:46 the *old* process logged `default shell.json load failed: 2` (`FileViewError.FileNotFound`) because `FileView { watchChanges: true }` still watches the packaged defaults while pacman replaces them. `QS_DISABLE_FILE_WATCHER` prevented the QML reload crash. Pid 1957 stayed up until the update’s planned kill.

### Expected

- After an update the bar and menus keep working, or come back as soon as the replacement process is actually usable — not as soon as IPC answers.
- A user who runs `omarchy restart shell` because the bar is missing must not be left with no shell.
- Packaged `shell.json` should not be FileView-watched during a pacman replace.

### Steps to reproduce

The update is only the trigger that invalidates qmlcache and then restarts. The failure is the cold PreferSynchronous compile plus a ping that returns too early.

1. `rm -rf ~/.cache/quickshell/qmlcache`
2. `journalctl -t omarchy-shell -f` in one terminal; `watch -n0.2 'ls ~/.cache/quickshell/qmlcache | wc -l'` in another.
3. `omarchy restart shell`
4. Observe: the command returns success immediately (`shell ping` at `Configuration Loaded`). The bar and menus are dead for tens of seconds. qmlcache files appear at about one per second. AT-SPI may log `Disabling unresponsive app`.
5. During that window, run `omarchy restart shell` again. The new pid logs `An instance of this configuration is already running.`, the compiling pid exits on the IPC kill, and nothing is left. Bar and menus stay dead until another restart.

On a fast CPU step 4 may be short enough to miss. Dropping the cache is the condition; `omarchy-update` that replaces `omarchy` / `omarchy-dev` is how it happens in real use.

### Suggested fix

- Load service plugins asynchronously (widgets already use `Component.Asynchronous`). PreferSynchronous on the UI thread is what makes the bar and menus disappear.
- `omarchy-restart-shell` should ping something later than IPC-up (idle `service-ready`, or a layer existing), and wait until the old pid is gone before `omarchy-launch-shell`.
- `omarchy-update-restart` should not print success before the restart, and should not `|| true` a failed one.
- Still do what #6748 asked: stop the shell before pacman writes `/usr/share/omarchy`, start it after. Also drop `watchChanges` on packaged `defaultsPath`.

Filed by Grok 4.6 via Grok Build.

issues.title: SUPER+C/V/X universal clipboard shortcuts fail with "send_key_state: key not found" when a non-Latin keyboard layout is active
issues.body:
### System details

Intel Core i5-8265U (ThinkPad X390, iGPU), Omarchy omarchy-dev 4.0.0.r1772.gf32ebbd-1, Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.1.8-arch1-3

### What's wrong?

With a multi-layout keyboard (e.g. `kb_layout = "us,th"`), pressing SUPER+C (also SUPER+V / SUPER+X) while the non-Latin layout is active pops up `Runtime error in lua: send_key_state: key not found` and nothing is copied. It works fine in the English layout.

## Steps to reproduce
1. `~/.config/hypr/input.lua`: `kb_layout = "us,th"`, `kb_options = "grp:caps_toggle"`
2. Switch to Thai (CapsLock), select text in any app, press SUPER+C
3. Error popup appears; clipboard unchanged. Switch back to English → works.

Notable: once SUPER+C succeeds once in English after a Hyprland reload, it starts working in Thai too until the next reload (keycode cache).

## Root cause (verified against Hyprland v0.56.2 source)
- `default/hypr/bindings/clipboard.lua` calls `hl.dsp.send_key_state({ mods = "CTRL", key = "C", ... })`.
- Hyprland's `resolveKeycode` (`src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsDispatchers.cpp`) maps key name `"C"` → keysym → keycode by scanning the keymap, but applies the **currently active layout group** (`xkb_state_update_mask(..., KB->m_modifiersState.group)`) before `xkb_state_key_get_one_sym()`. The Thai group has no Latin keysyms, so `"C"` is never found and the dispatcher raises `send_key_state: key not found` as a Lua runtime error.
- The keycode cache key (keyboard pointer + key name) doesn't include the group — explaining the "works after first success in English" behavior.
- Still present on Hyprland `main` (`src/keybinds/Resolver.cpp` uses `KB->m_xkbSymState`, which tracks the active group).

## Possible fixes
- Omarchy: pass evdev keycodes instead of names in `clipboard.lua` — `key = "code:46"` (C), `"code:47"` (V), `"code:45"` (X), `"code:110"` (Insert). `resolveKeycode` bypasses keysym resolution for `code:NN`, so the shortcuts work in any layout — mirroring a physical Ctrl+C press, which toolkits (GTK/Qt) match across layout groups.
- Hyprland (upstream): `resolveKeycode` should search all layout groups (or fall back to group 0) instead of only the active one.

issues.title: Apple Studio Display over USB4 flashes: stock preferred is 5K@120, then DP tunnel drops while Thunderbolt stays authorized
issues.body:
### System details

- **Machine:** HP ZBook X G1i 16 inch Mobile Workstation PC
- **CPU/iGPU:** Intel Arrow Lake-P (Arc Pro 130T/140T, `8086:7d51`)
- **dGPU:** NVIDIA RTX PRO 1000 Blackwell (`10de:2db8`), `nvidia-open-dkms 610.57.04-1`
- **Display:** Apple Studio Display XDR over USB4/Thunderbolt (authorized at 40 Gb/s). USB camera/audio/HID work even when video is gone.
- **Omarchy:** 4.0.0-1 (Quattro)
- **Kernel:** 7.1.8-arch1-3
- **Compositor:** Hyprland 0.56.2
- **Stock config:** `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` ships `hl.monitor({ output = "", mode = "preferred", position = "auto", scale = 1.25 })`

### What's wrong?

Connecting an Apple Studio Display over Thunderbolt/USB4 makes the external picture flash in and out. USB (camera, speakers, HID) and `boltctl` stay authorized. Only the DisplayPort tunnel (`card0-DP-1`) dies.

Two stacked problems:

1. **Stock `mode = "preferred"` picks 5120x2880@120.04Hz.** That is the first EDID mode. Hyprland brings the display up at 5K@120, scale 1.25, then loses it.

2. **The USB4 DP tunnel still drops even after pinning a sane mode.** `5120x2880@60` and `3840x2160@60` both went `disconnected` after ~20s. Kernel logs include `thunderbolt ... failed to reach state TB_PORT_UP` and `lost during suspend, disconnecting`. The Studio Display node sits at `power/autosuspend_delay_ms=15000` with `control=auto`. Forcing `control=on` on the Thunderbolt devices and the Arrow Lake USB-C root ports (`8086:7ec4` / `8086:7ec6`) stopped full TB disconnects, but `DP-1` still went disconnected while `0-1` stayed `runtime=active`.

This is an Intel USB4 / Thunderbolt 5 (Barlow Ridge JHL9480) path on Arrow Lake, not a dumb HDMI monitor. `thunderbolt.clx=Y` (CL0s) is on and not writable at runtime.

Omarchy's docs say an Intel Thunderbolt 4 machine should just work with a direct USB-C cable (https://learn.omacom.io/3/omacom/75/apple-displays-on-linux). On this Arrow Lake + Studio Display setup it does not.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh Omarchy 4.0.0-1 on an Intel USB4 laptop (here: HP ZBook X G1i).
2. Leave the default `monitors.lua` catch-all (`mode = "preferred"`).
3. Plug in an Apple Studio Display XDR over Thunderbolt/USB4.
4. `boltctl` shows the display authorized; `hyprctl monitors` shows `DP-1` at `5120x2880@120.04` with scale `1.25`.
5. After ~60 seconds the picture dies. `hyprctl` no longer lists `DP-1`. USB functions on the display keep working.
6. The display reappears at 120Hz and the cycle repeats.

### Expected

The Studio Display stays up. Prefer a stable 5K mode (5120x2880@60) rather than EDID-preferred 120Hz.

### Workaround attempted (not sufficient)

Pinned the Studio Display so stock `preferred` cannot select 120Hz (do not also leave a catch-all — see #7242):

```lua
hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", mode = "preferred", position = "0x0", scale = 1.25 })
hl.monitor({
  output = "desc:Apple Computer Inc Studio XDR",
  mode = "3840x2160@60",
  position = "auto",
  scale = 1.5,
  bitdepth = 8,
})
```

Plus a udev rule forcing Thunderbolt / USB-C root-port `power/control=on`. Video still drops after ~20s.

### Evidence

```
08:33:31  monitoraddedv2 DP-1 Apple Studio XDR  5120x2880@120.04  scale 1.25
08:34:32  monitorremovedv2 DP-1                  (no TB device-disconnect)
08:34:41  monitoradded again at 120.04Hz
08:34:57  pinned 5120x2880@60; still dropped ~20s later
08:40:00  thunderbolt: failed to reach state TB_PORT_UP / lost during suspend
08:40:06  replug: 3840x2160@60 scale 1.5; dropped again at 08:40:28
08:42:31  replug with TB power/control=on; DP-1 up then gone at 08:42:56
          while thunderbolt 0-1 stayed runtime=active / authorized
```

`omarchy debug` is listed in `omarchy --help` on 4.0.0-1 but there is no `omarchy-debug` binary, so no logs.omarchy.org URL.

### Suggested fix

- Do not use `mode = "preferred"` for Apple Studio / Pro Display XDR. Pin a 60Hz mode (and 2x scale at 5K) in stock defaults or `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch`.
- Disable Thunderbolt runtime suspend / CL0s for USB4 displays (udev + `thunderbolt.clx=N`), or document that native USB-C is not reliable on Arrow Lake and point at the DP+USB-A cable path already on the Omacom page.
- Update https://learn.omacom.io/3/omacom/75/apple-displays-on-linux — “Intel TB4, just plug USB-C” is not true on this Arrow Lake + Studio Display hardware.

issues.title: Dropbox widget shows wrong quota for Basic accounts with bonus space
issues.body:
### What happened

The Dropbox bar widget reports the wrong storage quota for Dropbox Basic accounts that carry bonus space.

My account shows **1.53 GB of 21.38 GB** on dropbox.com, but the widget shows **1.64 GB of 2 GB** — so it renders as ~82% full when the account is actually ~7% full.

### Cause

`shell/plugins/panels/dropbox/status.py` maps the plan name to a hardcoded quota:

```python
PLAN_QUOTAS = {
  "basic": 2_000_000_000,
  "plus": 2_000_000_000_000,
  ...
}
```

```python
quota = PLAN_QUOTAS.get(plan.lower(), 0)
```

`plan` comes from `subscription_type` in `~/.dropbox/info.json`, which is just `"Basic"`. But 2 GB is only the *starting* allocation for a Basic account. Referral bonuses (500 MB each, up to 16 GB, permanent) and older promos such as the 3 GB camera-upload bonus permanently raise the real quota. Mine adds up to 21.38 GB. Nothing in the plan name conveys this, so any long-standing Basic account is misreported.

The same applies in the other direction for Plus/Professional accounts with add-on storage.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Dropbox Basic account that earned referral or promo bonus space (real quota > 2 GB).
2. Log in via the Dropbox widget and let it sync.
3. Open the widget panel.
4. It reads `of 2 GB` instead of the account's actual quota, and the usage bar is proportionally wrong.

### Expected

The quota shown should match the account's real allocation, or the widget should omit the denominator when it cannot determine it, rather than assert a value it hasn't verified.

### Notes on fixing

The local daemon doesn't expose the quota — `dropbox-cli` has no such command, and `~/.dropbox/info.json` carries only the plan name. The authoritative figure comes from the Dropbox API (`/2/users/get_space_usage`, `allocation.allocated`), which needs an OAuth token, so a fully automatic fix means adding a token setup flow.

Cheaper options, in rough order of effort:

- Add an optional quota-override setting to the widget manifest so affected users can correct it (this is what I did locally, as a cloned plugin — a `quotaOverrideMB` integer setting passed through to `status.py`).
- Fall back to `quotaKnown: false` for `basic` specifically, since it's the one plan whose stated quota is routinely wrong, and show usage without a denominator.

Happy to open a PR for the override-setting approach if that direction is welcome.

### Related detail

`usedBytes` is also computed locally by `scan_dropbox()` walking the sync folder rather than read from Dropbox. It's close enough when everything is synced (1.64 GB vs 1.53 GB here, the difference being `.dropbox.cache`), but it will understate usage for anyone using selective sync. Same root cause: no API access.

### System

- Omarchy 4.0.0-1
- Dropbox 264.4.3421-1, dropbox-cli 2024.04.17-2
- Account type: Dropbox Basic with referral/promo bonus space

issues.title: Clipboard: selecting entry auto-pastes into focused terminal
issues.body:
## Problem

Selecting an entry from the clipboard manager (`omarchy.clipboard`) auto-pastes it into the focused terminal via `wtype -M shift -k Insert`. This is unexpected — users expect a clipboard manager to **copy** the selected entry to the clipboard, not immediately paste it.

The auto-paste is disruptive because:
- It inserts text into whatever terminal/app is focused without consent
- Users who just want to copy an older clipboard entry end up pasting it accidentally
- It differs from standard clipboard manager behavior (e.g.clipmenu, CopyQ)

## Expected Behavior

- **Enter / Click** → Copy selected entry to clipboard only (no paste)
- **Shift+Enter** → Copy and paste (Shift+Insert)
- **Alt+Enter** → Open entry in default app

## Actual Behavior

- **Enter / Click** → Copies AND auto-pastes into focused window
- **Shift+Enter** → Copies only (the expected copy-only behavior is swapped)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a terminal
2. Copy some text (e.g. `echo "hello"`)
3. Copy different text (e.g. `echo "world"`)
4. Open clipboard manager (default binding)
5. Select the first entry with Enter
6. "hello" is auto-pasted into the terminal

## Root Cause

In `Clipboard.qml`, the `activateIndex` (which copies + pastes) and `copyIndex` (copy only) are swapped relative to user expectations:

- Line ~388 (keyboard handler): Enter triggers `activateIndex` instead of `copyIndex`
- Line ~523 (mouse click handler): Click triggers `activateIndex` instead of `copyIndex`

## Workaround

I've cloned the plugin and swapped the call order in `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/mihai.clipboard/Clipboard.qml`:

```diff
# Keyboard handler (~line 388)
} else if (event.key === Qt.Key_Return || event.key === Qt.Key_Enter) {
  if (root.cursorActive && (event.modifiers & Qt.AltModifier)) root.openIndex(root.selectedIndex)
-  else if (root.cursorActive && (event.modifiers & Qt.ShiftModifier)) root.copyIndex(root.selectedIndex)
-  else if (root.cursorActive) root.activateIndex(root.selectedIndex)
+  else if (root.cursorActive && (event.modifiers & Qt.ShiftModifier)) root.activateIndex(root.selectedIndex)
+  else if (root.cursorActive) root.copyIndex(root.selectedIndex)
  else if (displayModel.count > 0) root.cursorActive = true

# Mouse click handler (~line 523)
onClicked: {
  root.cursorActive = true
  root.selectedIndex = row.index
-  root.activateIndex(row.index)
+  root.copyIndex(row.index)
}
```

## System Details

- **Omarchy version:** 4.0.0-1
- **CPU:** Intel Core i7-10750H
- **GPU:** Intel UHD Graphics / NVIDIA GTX 1650 Ti Mobile
- **Shell:** Quickshell with `omarchy.clipboard` plugin

## Suggestion

Consider making "copy only" the default action for Enter/Click, and requiring Shift+Enter for copy+paste. This matches the behavior of most clipboard managers and avoids accidental text insertion.

issues.title: Low battery notification can fire on boot after resuming from a suspend that drained the battery (Quickshell rewrite)
issues.body:
### System details

Lenovo V15 G3 ABA, Omarchy dev (4.0.0-1), quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7-1,  Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3 - 

### What's wrong?

After the laptop powers off because the battery ran out during suspend, the next boot can still show the "Time to recharge! Battery is down to X%" critical notification — even though the machine is now plugged in and charging.

## What was expected

No low-battery warning once the charger is connected and the battery is charging.

## Likely cause

In `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins/services/battery/Service.qml`, `checkBattery()` runs on a `Timer` with `triggeredOnStart: true`, so it evaluates battery state the instant Quickshell starts — before UPower has necessarily synced the real AC/charging state over DBus. If the very first read still reflects "discharging" at ≤10% (the state the battery was in right before the machine died), `shouldWarnLowBattery()` in `BatteryModel.js` fires the warning immediately, regardless of the charger actually being connected by then.

This is the same class of bug as two previously closed issues from the older bash/systemd-timer implementation:

- #2886 "False low battery notification on boot"
- #2968 "recharge battery notification appears at startup even with enough battery"

Both were closed months ago, but the battery-notification logic has since been rewritten to Quickshell/QML (`Service.qml` + `BatteryModel.js`), and the new code reintroduces the same startup race between the immediate check and UPower's DBus state settling

## Steps to reproduce

1. Let the battery run down while the laptop is suspended (or otherwise off) until it powers off completely.
2. Plug in the charger and boot.
3. Observe whether the "Time to recharge!" notification appears despite the device already charging.

This is intermittent (depends on how fast UPower reports the real state vs. the shell's first check), so it may not reproduce on every boot.

issues.title: Crash watcher reports normal 1Password window close as a crash
issues.body:
## What happened

After installing and opening 1Password, I closed its window using Super+W. Omarchy immediately displayed:

> Process crashed: 1password

The close was intentional and the 1Password log shows an orderly shutdown.

## Expected

Closing 1Password normally should not produce a critical crash notification.

## Evidence

System:

- Omarchy 4.0.0-1
- Hardware: Apple MacBook Pro (MacBookPro18,2), ARM64
- 1Password 8.12.0 ARM64

The 1Password log immediately before systemd-coredump recorded the event:

```text
Front end event: window closed
Front end event: app will quit
shutdown requested!
starting app shutdown
running shutdown hook...
Failed to prepare for requesting dump
```

systemd-coredump then recorded:

```text
Process: 1password
Signal: SIGTRAP
si_code: TRAP_BRKPT
Core file: none
Resource limits disable core dumping for process
```

There was no memory pressure or OOM kill. The app had synced successfully before being closed.

## Likely mechanism

`omarchy-crash-watch` announces every journal entry with the systemd-coredump message ID. It currently cannot distinguish this 1Password shutdown-time Crashpad SIGTRAP from an unexpected application crash.

This differs from #7785: that report involves a background `1password --lock` helper across suspend/resume. This report concerns closing the main GUI normally with Super+W.

## Reproduction

1. Launch 1Password 8.12.0 on ARM64.
2. Close its window using Super+W.
3. Observe the critical “Process crashed: 1password” notification.

Filed by GPT-5 via Codex.

issues.title: Bluetooth panel treats trusted-but-unbonded devices as paired and never retries pairing
issues.body:
### System details

Intel Xeon E-2176M, Intel UHD P630 + NVIDIA Quadro P2000 Mobile, Omarchy 4.0.0-1, bluez 5.87-2

### What's wrong?

If the first Bluetooth pair attempt fails, the panel never pairs that device again.

`omarchy-bluetooth-device pair` ignores a failed `bluetoothctl pair`, then always marks the address trusted:

https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/blob/quattro/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-device#L33-L38

```bash
pair)
  power_on
  timeout 20s bluetoothctl pair "$address" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  trust_device
  timeout 20s bluetoothctl connect "$address" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
```

The panel then treats `trusted` as already paired. Later clicks only `connect`:

https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml#L276-L279

```qml
function connectDevice(device) {
  if (!device || device.connected) return
  if (device.paired || device.bonded || device.trusted) runDeviceAction(device, "connect", "connecting")
  else runDeviceAction(device, "pair", "connecting")
}
```

Known devices are `paired || bonded || trusted`, and that list is labeled **PAIRED**:

https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Model.js#L111-L112

BlueZ **Trusted** is not a bond. After a failed pair the device looks remembered, and connect cannot succeed.

Hit this with a Logitech MX Master 2S (BLE HID). `bluetoothctl info` after using the panel:

```
Paired: no
Bonded: no
Trusted: yes
Connected: no
```

Same trap for any device whose first pair fails (not in pairing mode, timeout, etc.).

**Repro**

1. Super+Ctrl+B, Bluetooth on, wait for scan
2. Click a discovered device that is not actually pairable, or whose pair times out
3. Device moves under **PAIRED**; tooltip on the next click is Connect, not Pair
4. Further clicks never pair
5. `bluetoothctl info <addr>` shows Trusted yes, Paired/Bonded no

**Expected**

- Trust only after pairing succeeds
- If a device is not paired/bonded, the next click should pair, even if it is already trusted
- Do not put trusted-but-unbonded devices under **PAIRED**

**Suggested fix**

- In `pair`, do not `|| true` the pair; only `trust` after `Paired`/`Bonded` is yes
- In `connectDevice()`, pair unless `paired || bonded` — do not use `trusted` as a stand-in
- Keep trusted-unpaired devices visible if wanted, but retry pair instead of connect

Related but different: https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/discussions/7008 (MX series HID/LE scan). This issue is only the pairing state machine.

issues.title: omarchy setup security fingerprint fails instantly on Goodix 27c6:530c/533c/538c readers — no open libfprint driver exists
issues.body:
Dell Inspiron 5585, AMD Ryzen 7 3700U, Goodix 27c6:530c fingerprint reader, Omarchy dev (4.0.0.r1816.g43bfe9b).

## What's wrong?

`omarchy setup security fingerprint` on a Goodix 53xc-family reader (`27c6:530c` / `533c` / `538c`, found in Dell machines) detects the sensor, installs `fprintd` + stock `libfprint`, then fails within a second:

```
$ fprintd-list "$USER"
No devices available            # exit 1

$ sudo fprintd-enroll "$USER"
Impossible to enroll: No devices available   # exit 1
```

The wizard prints "Enrollment failed. Please try again." and exits 1. Retrying can never succeed: stock libfprint has no driver for these ids at all — the `goodixmoc` id table starts at `27c6:5840`, and `530c`/`533c`/`538c` are absent from every release and from master. `omarchy-hw-fingerprint` correctly detects the reader beforehand (vendor 27c6, no kernel driver bound), which is exactly what makes the instant enrollment failure look transient instead of structural.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Use a Dell laptop with a Goodix `27c6:530c` (or `533c`/`538c`) reader
2. Run Setup > Security > Fingerprint (or `omarchy setup security fingerprint`)
3. Enrollment fails immediately with no actionable message

## What works

Dell ships a proprietary Linux TOD driver for this family, repackaged in the AUR as `libfprint-goodix-53xc` (closed binary from Dell's Ubuntu archive, `dell.archive.canonical.com`) on top of `libfprint-tod` (open libfprint fork with a vendor-plugin interface). With both installed and fprintd restarted, the device is claimed and enrollment works through the wizard's normal flow:

```
fprintd[...]: Creating TOD wrapper for goodix-tod (Goodix Fingerprint Sensor 53xc) driver
$ sudo fprintd-enroll
Using device /net/reactivated/Fprint/Device/1
Enroll result: enroll-stage-passed ...
```

I verified the blob's compiled id table is exactly `{27c6:530c, 27c6:533c, 27c6:538c}` (its udev rule also lists `5840`, which the open `goodixmoc` driver already covers). No PAM changes are needed — `pam_fprintd.so` talks to fprintd over D-Bus regardless of which driver loads underneath.

Two usage quirks worth knowing for this sensor: it is a **press** sensor (finger flat, hold ~1s per stage), and its firmware temporarily disables itself (`Device disabled to prevent overheating`) after repeated touches, recovering after a cool-down or reboot — rapid retry loops make the lockout longer (same behavior behind #7179).

Related: #1590 asked about `27c6:533c` and was closed hoping for an upstream libfprint driver — these ids are still absent from libfprint master today. #7483 / #7667 cover the same shape of problem for an ELAN reader.

issues.title: 1Password floating window is left off-screen after a monitor is disabled; relaunch focuses the invisible window
issues.body:
### System details

AMD Ryzen 7 5825U + Radeon (Barcelo), Omarchy 4.0.0-1, Hyprland 0.56.2 (v0.56.2, commit efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f), Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3, 1password 8.12.32-33.

`omarchy-debug` output is omitted here because it includes hostname and other machine-identifying fields.

### What's wrong?

Omarchy's default 1Password window rule tags the app `floating-window`. After a multi-output layout collapses to a single remaining display (the other HDMI output is disabled), the 1Password float stays at its old global coordinates, which are now off-screen. The window is mapped, not hidden, and on the current workspace — it just is not on any enabled monitor. Super+Shift+/ / `omarchy launch 1password` then looks like a no-op because 1Password is single-instance and focuses that existing invisible window.

This is a placement bug, not a 1Password crash. Tiled windows on the same session were relocated onto the remaining output; this float was not.

## Expected

A 1Password window tagged `floating-window` should remain visible on an enabled monitor. After an output is disabled, Omarchy's `center = true` rule should put it on the remaining display (or Hyprland should clamp it there). A later launch should show a window the user can see.

## Actual

- Only HDMI-A-1 was enabled: 1920×1080 at `(0,0)`.
- HDMI-A-2 (4K desktop) was disabled.
- Hyprland reported the 1Password client as mapped, not hidden, floating, size `875×600` (exactly the `floating-window` size), on the active workspace, at `[-1397, 225]`.
- Visible range of the remaining output is x=0–1920. The window occupied x=-1397 to -522, entirely to the left of the screen.
- `-1397` is the centered X for an 875-wide window on a 1920-wide output whose origin was at `-1920`: `-1920 + (1920-875)/2 = -1397.5`.
- 1Password's own saved window state still said on-screen bounds on a 1920×1080 display. The compositor overrode that because of the float tag.
- Each subsequent launch logged `1Password is already running, closing.` and exited. Autostart had already started `1password --silent`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install 1Password (`omarchy install 1password` / `omarchy-install-service-1password`) so autostart runs `1password --silent` and the default app rule applies.
2. Use two HDMI outputs. Let 1Password map its main window (unlock if needed) so the `floating-window` rule floats and sizes it to 875×600.
3. Disable one output so a single 1080p HDMI display remains at `(0,0)` (clamshell / KVM / "away" style layout is enough; the exact helper does not matter).
4. Press Super+Shift+/ or run `uwsm-app -- 1password`.
5. Observe: no visible window. `hyprctl clients` still shows a mapped 1Password float whose `at` is outside the remaining output.

## Omarchy config implicated

[`default/hypr/apps/1password.lua`](https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/blob/quattro/default/hypr/apps/1password.lua) tags 1Password as a float:

```lua
o.window("^(1[p|P]assword)$", { no_screen_share = true, tag = "+floating-window" })
```

[`default/hypr/apps/system.lua`](https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/blob/quattro/default/hypr/apps/system.lua) then applies:

```lua
o.window({ tag = "floating-window" }, { float = true })
o.window({ tag = "floating-window" }, { center = true })
o.window({ tag = "floating-window" }, { size = { 875, 600 } })
```

`center` appears to apply on map, not when the monitor layout later changes. Hyprland keeps the float's global coordinates; disabling the output that those coordinates belonged to strands the window. Bitwarden uses the same `+floating-window` tag and is likely in the same class, though this report only observed 1Password.

Related but not the same: #7160 (popped-out `SUPER+O` windows keep an old monitor-relative offset when moved). Same "global float coords survive a layout change" mechanism; this one is triggered by disabling a monitor under the default password-manager float rule, and is made unrecoverable by 1Password's single-instance launch.

## Suggested direction

When an output is disabled, recenter (or clamp) clients tagged `floating-window` onto a still-enabled monitor. Alternatively, `omarchy-launch-1password` could detect an existing mapped 1Password window whose box does not intersect any enabled output and `centerwindow` / move it before relying on the already-running instance.

## Workaround

Kill the running 1Password process and launch it again on the remaining output. If the layout does not change again, the new map is centered on-screen.

issues.title: [Quattro] omarchy-launch-screensaver creates focus-check race condition on 3+ monitor setups causing immediate self-termination
issues.body:
### System details
- **Hardware**: Framework Desktop, AMD Ryzen AI Max 395 (Radeon 8060S Graphics)
- **Omarchy Version**: 4.0.0-1 (Quattro)
- **Hyprland Configuration**: Lua parser (`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`)
- **Display Setup**: 3 monitors (`DP-1` portrait, `HDMI-A-1` ultrawide, `DP-4` landscape) vs 2 monitors tested
- **Terminal**: Kitty

### What's wrong?
On multi-monitor setups with 3 or more displays, `omarchy-launch-screensaver` triggers and then immediately self-terminates after a few seconds without any user interaction. On a 2-monitor system with identical Omarchy Quattro configuration, the screensaver runs as expected.

When the screensavers self-terminate, `omarchy-shell`'s idle manager (`Service.qml`) interprets the closed windows as a manual dismissal, issues `omarchy-system-wake`, and cancels the idle sequence—preventing `idle.lock` (300s) and display DPMS power-down from ever activating.

### Mechanism & Root Cause

1. **Sequential Output Launch Loop**:
   In `/usr/bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver`, screensavers are spawned sequentially across all connected displays:
   ```bash
   for m in $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[].name'); do
     hypr_focus_monitor "$m"
     case $terminal in ... esac
     wait_for_screensaver_window
   done
   hypr_focus_monitor "$focused"
   ```
   Each monitor iteration focuses the monitor, spawns the terminal screensaver window, and waits for the corresponding socket2 `openwindow` event.

2. **The 3+ Monitor Timing Race**:
   In `/usr/bin/omarchy-screensaver`, the main loop starts checking focus immediately with a 1-second timeout:
   ```bash
   while pgrep -t "${tty#/dev/}" -x ttfx >/dev/null; do
     if read -n1 -t 1 || ! screensaver_in_focus; then
       exit_screensaver
     fi
   done
   ```
   - On a **2-monitor system**, the loop completes quickly enough that both windows map and focus is restored to the primary monitor within ~1 second.
   - On a **3+ monitor system**, cycling through all three displays takes 2–4 seconds.
   - While the launcher is busy focusing Monitor 2 and Monitor 3, Monitor 1's screensaver process reaches its first 1-second timeout and evaluates `screensaver_in_focus`.

3. **Global Active Window Query**:
   `screensaver_in_focus()` checks global compositor focus:
   ```bash
   screensaver_in_focus() {
     hyprctl activewindow -j | jq -e '.class == "org.omarchy.screensaver"' >/dev/null 2>&1
   }
   ```
   Because compositor focus is actively transitioning to Monitor 2/3 (or momentarily lands on existing windows on those workspaces before the screensaver terminal is mapped), Monitor 1 sees that `activewindow` is not its own screensaver class. `! screensaver_in_focus` evaluates to true, executing `exit_screensaver` (`pkill -f org.omarchy.screensaver`) and killing all screensavers across all monitors.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Connect 3 displays with active application windows on each workspace.
2. Trigger the screensaver via `omarchy-launch-screensaver` or wait for `idle.screensaver` (150s).
3. Observe Monitor 1 launch, followed by Monitor 2/3, followed by immediate teardown within 3–6 seconds without user input.

### Suggested Solutions
1. **Startup Grace Period**: Add an initial grace period (e.g. 5–6 seconds) to `omarchy-screensaver` before evaluating `screensaver_in_focus`, giving multi-monitor launch loops sufficient time to finish mapping all screens.
2. **Event-Driven Dismissal**: Rather than polling global `activewindow` every second in each terminal process, rely on compositor idle/wake notifications from `omarchy-shell` and terminal keypress/signal handlers to handle screensaver dismissal.

> Filed by Gemini via Antigravity CLI.

issues.title: omarchy-theme-set-browser hangs when brave-origin is running but Brave is not (pgrep -x brave false-positive)
issues.body:
### System details

AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (Navi 48), Omarchy 4.0.0.r1827.gb86d450-1, kernel 7.1.8-arch1-3.
Both `brave-bin 1:1.93.137-1` and `brave-origin-bin 1:1.93.137-1` installed; only brave-origin is ever run.

### What's wrong?

`omarchy update` hangs indefinitely inside a migration. The migration never returns, so `omarchy-migrate` never writes its marker file, and that migration plus every migration after it stays pending forever — each subsequent `omarchy update` re-runs it and hangs again.

In my case migration `1787481315` ("Re-stage the current theme so an installed theme's code is dropped") hung. It calls `omarchy-theme-refresh` → `omarchy-theme-set`, which blocks on `run_parallel`'s `wait` in the post-theme command list. But the migration is incidental — anything that reaches `omarchy-theme-set-browser` hangs the same way.

The culprit is the last-but-one line of `bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser`:

```bash
refresh_running_browser brave brave        # guard: pgrep -x brave
```

`refresh_running_browser` guards on `pgrep -x brave`. **brave-origin's processes are all named plain `brave`** — that is exactly the collision the very next line already documents:

```bash
# Match on the binary path: the running process is named plain "brave", and a
# bare -f brave-origin pattern would also match the installer's own terminal.
refresh_running_browser /opt/brave-origin-bin/ brave-origin -f
```

So with brave-origin running and Brave not running, `pgrep -x brave` matches (27 processes here, all children of `/opt/brave-origin-bin/brave`), the guard passes, and the script then launches **the other binary**, `/usr/bin/brave` (from `brave-bin`, `/opt/brave-bin/`). With `--no-startup-window` that new instance has no window to close, never exits, and `run_parallel`'s `wait` blocks on it forever.

This is the same failure mode as #4772, which was fixed by adding the `pgrep` guard. This case slips past that fix because the guard produces a false positive across two different browsers that share a process name.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install both `brave-bin` and `brave-origin-bin`.
2. Launch brave-origin. Do not launch Brave.
3. Run `omarchy theme set <any-theme>` (or `omarchy update` with a pending migration that re-stages the theme).
4. It hangs. `ps` shows a stray `/usr/bin/brave --refresh-platform-policy --no-startup-window`. Killing it lets the update continue.

### Diagnostics

Timing each of the 14 `post_theme_commands` individually, stdin from `/dev/null`:

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `omarchy-theme-set-browser` | **timeout at 25s** |
| all 13 others | ≤ 3s, rc=0 |

Narrowing to the two Brave branches:

```
$ timeout 10 brave        --refresh-platform-policy --no-startup-window   # rc=124 (hang)
$ timeout 10 brave-origin --refresh-platform-policy --no-startup-window   # rc=0   (0s)
```

Confirming the false positive:

```
$ pgrep -xc brave
27
$ pgrep -af brave | grep -v origin      # is real Brave running?
(nothing)
$ readlink -f /usr/bin/brave /usr/bin/brave-origin
/usr/bin/brave
/usr/bin/brave-origin
```

After quitting brave-origin, `omarchy-migrate` ran straight through with no hang.

Note: `contributing.md` points at `omarchy debug --no-sudo --print` for diagnostics, but that command does not exist on 4.0.0 (`Unknown Omarchy command: omarchy debug`), so the details above are gathered by hand.

### Suggested fix

Match the plain-Brave branch on its binary path, the way the brave-origin branch already does, so the two cannot alias each other:

```bash
refresh_running_browser /opt/brave-bin/ brave -f
```

A `timeout` around the `"$command" --refresh-platform-policy` call would also cap the damage generally — the policy is picked up on next launch anyway, so there is nothing to lose by giving up on it.

issues.title: Full-disk install: password set under a non-US keyboard layout can be untypeable at the LUKS boot prompt
issues.body:
### Repro (hit on real hardware — Dell Inspiron 14 5435, current ISO, 2026-08-25)

1. AZERTY laptop; select the French keyboard layout in the installer
2. choose full-disk install; set a password containing digits (on AZERTY, digits are the *shifted* top row)
3. install completes; reboot
4. at the LUKS unlock prompt the password is rejected on every attempt

### What appears to happen

The installer honors the selected layout while the password is set, but the early-boot LUKS prompt reads US QWERTY (the chosen keymap doesn't reach the initramfs). A digits-only password enrolled under French AZERTY becomes untypeable: shifted-row digits don't exist under the boot prompt's map, and unshifted keys produce different characters than were enrolled. QWERTY-translation attempts at the prompt (unshifted digits, a/q z/w m swaps) also failed, consistent with the enrolled bytes being the layout-correct characters.

### Impact

Locked out of a fresh install, no recovery except reinstalling. A first-time user experiences this as “Omarchy won't take my password” with nothing pointing at the cause. AZERTY (France/Belgium), QWERTZ (DACH), and other remapped layouts are all exposed — and it only bites people who did the security-conscious thing and put digits in their passphrase.

### Workaround that got us through

Reinstall with a passphrase using only layout-stable keys (lowercase letters, avoiding a/q/z/w/m, no digits or symbols).

### Possible directions

- propagate the installer's selected layout into the initramfs so the LUKS prompt matches enrollment
- or warn at password-set time when the passphrase contains characters that move across layouts
- or at minimum a note in the manual for non-US layouts

Happy to retest any fix on the same hardware.

issues.title: A bare click in the capture picker snaps to the whole monitor instead of the highlighted window
issues.body:
In `smart` mode (the default for both `omarchy screenshot` and `omarchy capture screenrecording`), slurp is fed the monitor and window rectangles and highlights the one under the pointer. Click a window without dragging and you get the whole monitor instead of the window that was highlighted.

## Why

`omarchy-capture-region` treats a selection under 20px² as a bare click and snaps it to a rectangle itself:

```bash
while IFS= read -r rect; do
  ...
  if ((click_x >= rect_x && click_x < rect_x + rect_width && ...)); then
    SELECTION="${rect_x},${rect_y} ${rect_width}x${rect_height}"
    break
  fi
done <<<"$RECTS"
```

It takes the **first** containing rectangle. `$RECTS` comes from `get_rectangles()`, which prints `monitor_rects` before `window_rects`, and a monitor contains every click on it — so the loop always stops on the monitor and never reaches the windows behind it.

The rest of the file already knows the right rule. `resolve_rect_at()` picks the *smallest* containing rectangle, with the comment "slurp highlights the smallest box containing the point and keeps the first one on a tie, so overlapping rectangles resolve the same way here", and `geo_at_cursor()` deliberately tries `window_rects` before `monitor_rects` for the same reason. Only the click-snap path disagrees.

## Reproduce

Press the screenshot key, hover a window until slurp highlights it, and click without dragging. The saved PNG is the full monitor.

Same for `omarchy capture screenrecording` — the recording is started with `-w <monitor geometry>` rather than the window's.

issues.title: omarchy theme set / omarchy update hangs indefinitely in omarchy-theme-set-keyboard-f16 with a Keychron K8 Pro attached
issues.body:
### System details

AMD Ryzen 7 9700X, AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT, Omarchy 4.0.1-1, kernel 7.1.8-arch1-3, Hyprland 0.56.2, qmk-hid 0.1.11-3 (explicitly installed), keyboard: Keychron K8 Pro (QMK/VIA firmware)

### What's wrong?

# What's wrong?
With a Keychron K8 Pro (QMK/VIA keyboard) attached over USB, every `omarchy theme set <theme>` blocks forever after printing a single line (`Effect: 1`). Because the 4.0.1 update migration `1787481315` re-stages the current theme via `omarchy-theme-refresh`, `omarchy update` wedged at that migration on every retry until I unplugged the keyboard — it looked like a bricked update.

## Process tree while stuck (two independent instances, same spot)

```
bash -lc 'theme=$(omarchy-theme-switcher); ... omarchy-theme-set "$theme"'
└─ omarchy-theme-set tokyo-night
   └─ omarchy-theme-set-keyboard
      └─ omarchy-theme-set-keyboard-f16      <- STAT do_wait
         └─ qmk_hid via --rgb-hue 212        <- never exits
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Attach a Keychron K8 Pro over USB
2. Run `omarchy theme set tokyo-night`
3. Observe: prints `Effect: 1`, then hangs forever
4. Unplug the keyboard, re-run: completes immediately

Direct reproduction of the blocking call:

```
$ timeout 5 qmk_hid via --rgb-hue 100   # K8 Pro attached
[killed at timeout, exit 124]
```

Side note for anyone debugging this from user reports: the f16 script only redirects stderr of the qmk_hid calls, so qmk_hid's own stdout response (`Effect: 1`) lands in the terminal and reads like output from whatever step preceded the hang.

Context: qmk-hid was not preinstalled on my system — I added it manually while configuring the K8 Pro (`pacman -S qmk-hid`). `omarchy-theme-set-keyboard-f16` then picked it up opportunistically and applied theme colors to the keyboard on every theme change. That is reasonable behavior; the problem is only that nothing bounds it.

## Analysis

Neither keyboard theming script detects actual hardware. The entire guard in `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-keyboard-f16` is:

```bash
if omarchy-cmd-present qmk_hid && [[ -f $FRAMEWORK16_THEME ]]; then
```

i.e. binary present + theme ships a `keyboard.rgb`, then fire five unbounded `qmk_hid` calls. Despite the name, nothing checks for a Framework 16 or any VIA device. The sibling `omarchy-theme-set-keyboard-asus-rog` has the identical pattern (`asusctl` present + rgb file) but gets away with it because `asusctl` fails fast on foreign hardware — `qmk_hid` instead blocks indefinitely on a non-responsive HID device.

(`omarchy-debug` is not available on my installed version to attach its output.)

## Expected

Theme application completes (or the keyboard step fails fast) regardless of what other HID devices are attached.

## Suggested fix

- Wrap the five `qmk_hid` invocations in `timeout`, matching the pattern used elsewhere in Omarchy's scripts (e.g. `shell_ipc()` uses `timeout 2`).
- Optionally verify an actual VIA-capable device responds before invoking `qmk_hid`.

Separately, qmk-hid itself hanging forever instead of erroring is arguably an upstream bug — happy to file there too.

issues.title: Quickshell SIGSEGV tearing down the workspaces Repeater when Hyprland moves workspaces between monitors
issues.body:
## What happened

Quickshell died with SIGSEGV while Hyprland was shuffling workspaces between monitors during a monitor-profile change. The shell restarted automatically; no user data was lost.

The fault is in the bar's workspaces widget. `plugins/bar/widgets/Workspaces.qml` rebuilds its `Repeater` from inside Quickshell's own mid-mutation `valuesChanged` emit, and its delegates hold live `HyprlandWorkspace` QObject references.

## Symbolized stack

Arch debuginfod, Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2. `si_addr = 0x3e8001ad392` (garbage pointer, not null).

```
#5  QV4::Value::as<QV4::QObjectWrapper>            qv4heap_p.h:46          <-- SEGV
#7  QV4::WeakValue::free                           qv4persistent.cpp:455
#10 QQmlData::destroyed                            qqmlengine.cpp:1427
#11 QObject::~QObject                              qobject.cpp:1084
#12 QQmlDMListAccessorData::~QQmlDMListAccessorData qqmldmlistaccessordata.cpp:25
#13 QQmlDelegateModelPrivate::release              qqmldelegatemodel.cpp:633
#14 QQuickRepeater::clear                          qquickrepeater.cpp:422
#15 QQuickRepeater::setModel                       qquickrepeater.cpp:179
#17 QQmlPropertyPrivate::write                     qqmlproperty.cpp:1978
#21 QQmlBinding::update                            qqmlbinding.cpp:166
#22 QQmlNotifier::emitNotify                       qqmlnotifier.cpp:75
#24 UntypedObjectModel::valuesChanged              moc_model.cpp:195
#25 ObjectModel<HyprlandWorkspace>::insertObject   core/model.hpp:93       <-- emit mid-insert
#26 ObjectModel<HyprlandWorkspace>::insertObjectSorted
#27 HyprlandIpc::onEvent                           ipc/connection.cpp:349
#28 HyprlandIpc::eventSocketReady                  ipc/connection.cpp:136
#33 QAbstractSocketPrivate::canReadNotification    qabstractsocket.cpp:673
```

Frame 27 locals identify the event exactly:

```
name    = "7"
existed = false
```

So Quickshell had no workspace 7, created one, and emitted `valuesChanged()` from inside `insertObject` while the model list was still being mutated. That synchronous emit re-enters QML, which tears the whole Repeater down.

## Why the Repeater is torn down at all

`plugins/bar/widgets/Workspaces.qml:51`:

```qml
Repeater {
  model: root.workspaceIds()
```

`workspaceIds()` reads `Hyprland.workspaces.values`, so the binding is subscribed to `valuesChanged`, and it returns a **fresh JS array on every evaluation**. Every workspace add/remove therefore assigns a new model and triggers a full `setModel` → `clear()` → destroy-all-delegates cycle — from inside the mid-mutation emit. `GridLayout.columns` (line 45) binds the same signal.

The delegate holds a live QObject (line 55):

```qml
readonly property var workspace: root.workspaceById(modelData)
readonly property bool occupied: workspace !== null && workspace.toplevels.values.length > 0
```

Inference, not proven from the frames: the delegate for `modelData == 7` still held a `QObjectWrapper` for the `HyprlandWorkspace` destroyed by the earlier `destroyworkspace>>7`. Destroying that delegate data inside the emit walks a stale V4 persistent slot, which matches the garbage `si_addr` rather than a null deref. The delegate identity is not recoverable from the available frames.

## Trigger / reproduction

Framework Laptop 13 with two external displays, lid transition causing `hyprmoncfgd` to re-apply the "Desktop Mode" monitor profile while the lock screen was coming up. Quickshell's own log tail immediately before the crash:

```
21:22:02  omarchy lock ... secure=true
21:22:03  hyprmoncfgd: applied profile "Desktop Mode"; monitoradded:eDP-1
          destroyworkspace>>7
          monitoradded>>eDP-1
          moveworkspace>>1,DP-2
          destroyworkspace>>8
          moveworkspace>>3,DP-2
          workspace>>7                    <-- recreates ws 7 (existed=false)
          moveworkspace>>5,DP-2
          moveworkspace>>7,DP-2
          monitorremoved>>eDP-1
21:22:06  SIGSEGV
```

Any monitor add/remove that makes Hyprland destroy and recreate workspaces should reach this. It does not require the lock screen — the lock screen only supplied the monitor churn here.

## Not a recent regression

The same crash class was recorded on this machine on 2026-08-16 (`QQuickRepeater::regenerate` / `setModel`) under `quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7` and Qt 6.11.1, before the 2026-08-25 switch to `quickshell 0.3.1`. `Workspaces.qml` is byte-identical to current `basecamp/omarchy` HEAD.

## Relationship to #6952

#6952 is the same *class* — a `Repeater` rebuilt from a model-mutation signal with delegates holding live Quickshell QObjects — but not the same bug. That one is PipeWire-driven and faults on the **incubation** path (`VDMListDelegateDataType::createMissingProperties`, `qqmldmlistaccessordata_p.h:222`, null `QObject*` row). This one is Hyprland-IPC-driven and faults on the **destruction** path (`QQmlDMListAccessorData` dtor → `QV4::WeakValue::free`), in a different file. Filing separately rather than as a comment there, but they likely want the same fix pattern.

## Suggested fix

The codebase already has the defense in two places:

- `plugins/panels/bluetooth/Model.js` `deviceRow()` — primitives-only rows, commented *"delegates never hold Device QObject wrappers … which segfaults quickshell"*, with actions re-resolving the live object via `deviceFor()`.
- `plugins/notifications/Service.qml:189` — `Qt.callLater` to avoid mutating a model while a Repeater is mid-incubation.

`Workspaces.qml` does neither. Projecting the delegate to primitives (`id`, `occupied`, `focused`) and resolving the `HyprlandWorkspace` only at press time would remove the dangling wrapper, and deferring the model reassignment with `Qt.callLater` would get the reassignment out of Quickshell's mid-mutation emit. Keeping the model array stable when the id set is unchanged would also cut most of the teardown churn, since `workspaceIds()` returns `[1..5]` plus extras and usually produces an identical list.

Arguably `ObjectModel::insertObject` emitting `valuesChanged()` before the insert has settled deserves an upstream Quickshell report too.

## System

```
Omarchy       4.0.1-1 (stable channel)
quickshell    0.3.1-1
qt6-declarative 6.11.2-1
qt6-base      6.11.2-2
hyprland      0.56.2-1
kernel        7.1.9-arch1-2
hardware      Framework Laptop 13 (AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series)
monitors      DP-2 ASUS PG32UCDP 3840x2160@120, DP-7 PanaScope PX329 2560x1440@144, eDP-1 internal
```

Crash report on the reporting machine: `~/.cache/quickshell/crashes/pc12k0ckt` (PID 1758098, 2026-08-26 21:22:06 CEST). `omarchy debug` is not available in 4.0.1, so the above was collected by hand.

---
