issues.title: `omarchy display text size` breaks 1Password's fixed-size dialogs (root cause of #2016)
issues.body:
## Summary

`omarchy display text size` (and the Display panel's Text size slider) sets GNOME's `text-scaling-factor`. Chromium/Electron apps **multiply that factor into their device scale factor**, which shrinks the usable layout area of any fixed-size window by the same factor. 1Password's SSH authorization prompt is such a window — ~402x371 logical px with min size = max size — so at text size 16 (factor 1.3636) about 26% of the dialog's content, including the authorize button, is pushed off-window.

This is the root cause behind #2016 ("1Password authorization window cut off"), which was closed without a fix and attributed to a 1Password regression. It also explains the confusing per-machine variance reported there (same monitor scale, different outcome): the trigger is the *text* scale, not the monitor scale.

## Reproduce

1. `omarchy display text size 16` (any value above 12 works; bigger is worse)
2. Restart 1Password so it picks the factor up, enable its SSH agent
3. Trigger any SSH signature, e.g. without touching the network:
   ```bash
   ssh-add -L > /tmp/k.pub
   SSH_AUTH_SOCK=~/.1password/agent.sock ssh-keygen -Y sign -f /tmp/k.pub -U -n test /etc/hostname
   ```
4. The authorization dialog appears with its checkbox/buttons clipped.

The dialog cannot be rescued compositor-side: it reports min size = max size, so `size` window rules and `hl.dsp.window.resize(...)` are silently ignored — which is why the window-rule attempts in #2016 only ever affected the main window.

## Root cause, measured

Chromium computes its device scale on Wayland as `monitor scale x text-scaling-factor`. Verified with a scratch Chromium and CDP (`Runtime.evaluate` on `window.devicePixelRatio` via `--remote-debugging-port`), on a 2x monitor with text size 16 (factor 1.3636):

| Launch | devicePixelRatio |
|---|---|
| baseline | **2.71875** (= 2 x 1.36) |
| `GDK_DPI_SCALE=0.733` | 2.71875 — no effect on Chromium |
| `--force-device-scale-factor=2` | 4.0 — multiplies, worse |
| `GSETTINGS_BACKEND=memory` | **2.0 — fixed** |

The window frame stays at its fixed logical size while the app lays out at the inflated DPR, so the dialog's 402 logical px become `402 x 2 / 2.72 ≈ 295` CSS px of layout — content designed for 402 gets clipped. The same math applies to the main window (the 875x600 `floating-window` tag default becomes ~643 effective px — the "1Password window too small" complaints).

## Fix

Launch 1Password with `GSETTINGS_BACKEND=memory`: in-process gsettings reads come back as defaults, so it renders at the plain monitor scale and every fixed-size dialog gets its full designed layout (the SSH prompt even sizes itself taller, 402x426 here, everything visible). Dark/light detection is portal-based and keeps working.

One gotcha makes placement non-obvious: **1Password rewrites `~/.config/autostart/1password.desktop` on startup**, so the env cannot live in the autostart desktop file. Since Omarchy runs XDG autostart entries as `app-<name>@autostart.service` units, a systemd user drop-in survives:

```ini
# /etc/systemd/user/app-1password@autostart.service.d/text-scaling.conf
[Service]
Environment=GSETTINGS_BACKEND=memory
```

PR incoming that applies this on every launch path (launcher, installer, desktop override, packaged autostart drop-in, migration). Bitwarden and other Electron apps with fixed-size dialogs have the same exposure; the trade-off (the app renders at standard size instead of following the text scale; in-app Ctrl+= compensates) is documented in the drop-in.

The proper fix belongs to 1Password (size fixed dialogs in CSS px, or make them resizable) — worth reporting upstream too, but Omarchy controls the trigger, so a guard here helps users today.

## Environment

- Omarchy 4.0.1-1, Hyprland 0.56.2
- 1Password 8.12.32 (conceptually matches the 8.11.x reports in #2016)
- Monitor 3840x2160 @ scale 2; `text-scaling-factor` 1.3636 (set by `omarchy display text size 16`)

(No screenshot: Omarchy correctly tags 1Password `no_screen_share`, captures come out black.)

issues.title: Hyprland reload-pause guard silently fails to prevent mid-update Lua reload — emergency mode banner during omarchy update
issues.body:
## What happened

During `omarchy update` (4.0.0-1 → 4.0.1-1), Hyprland's Lua config reloaded in the middle of the pacman transaction, exactly while pacman was replacing the `omarchy-settings` files. For a moment `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/bootstrap.lua` did not exist on disk, so the `dofile` in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` failed, no binds were registered, and Hyprland 0.56's emergency mode tripped:

```
Emergency mode tripped: A lua config error resulted in no binds being registered. Emergency binds active: SUPER + Q → any known terminal, SUPER + R → hyprland-run, SUPER + M → Exit
Your config has errors:
cannot open /usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/bootstrap.lua: No such file or directory
stack traceback:
        [C]: in global 'dofile'
```

The banner sat on top of every workspace for the rest of the update (screenshot attached).

## What I expected

`10-omarchy-hyprland-reload-pause.hook` exists to prevent exactly this: it runs `omarchy-hyprland-reload-guard pause` as a PreTransaction hook, which is supposed to set `misc.disable_autoreload = true` and `debug.suppress_errors = true` on every running instance so no reload can observe the half-replaced tree.

## Timeline (from `/var/log/pacman.log` and the user journal)

- `23:51:47` — `10-omarchy-hyprland-reload-pause.hook` runs. The guard's state file was created in `/run/omarchy/hyprland-reload-guard/` with the correct saved option values, so the script ran and its two `getoption` reads succeeded.
- `23:52:04–05` — `omarchy-settings` and `omarchy` upgraded (files replaced).
- `23:52:05` — the user journal shows Hyprland recompiling its keymap (xkbcomp warnings), the fingerprint of a config reload. The emergency banner appeared at this point and referenced the transiently missing `bootstrap.lua`.

## Why I believe the pause silently failed

I verified the guard's mechanism works when invoked as the session user:

- `hyprctl eval 'hl.config({ misc = { disable_autoreload = true }, debug = { suppress_errors = true } })'` succeeds and `getoption` confirms the values.
- With that pause active, neither `touch` nor a real rewrite of `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` or `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua` triggers a reload. So `disable_autoreload` does block file-triggered reloads, including for Lua modules.

Yet on the real run the reload fired 17 seconds after the pause hook. The pause path in `omarchy-hyprland-reload-guard` is:

```bash
hyprctl_instance "$runtime_dir" "$signature" eval \
  'hl.config({ misc = { disable_autoreload = true }, debug = { suppress_errors = true } })' \
  >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
```

Every failure mode of that `eval` — running as root against the user instance included — is swallowed by `>/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, so if it is rejected or errors, the "pause" is silently a no-op while the state file still gets written (the state file is created *before* the eval, from the two successful `getoption` reads). That matches the observed behavior exactly: state file present, options not actually set, reload not prevented.

## Suggestion

After the pause eval, read the option back and verify it is actually `true`; log loudly (the hook output surfaces in the pacman transcript) when it is not. The resume path has the same silent-failure shape and would benefit from the same check.

## System

- Omarchy 4.0.1-1, hyprland 0.56.2-1 (Arch package)
- CPU: Intel Core i7-14650HX
- GPU: Intel Raptor Lake-S UHD + NVIDIA RTX 4080 Max-Q (hybrid), nvidia-dkms 610.57.04
- Kernel: 7.1.8-arch1-3 → 7.1.9-arch1-2 during the affected update

issues.title: tsl and hsl silently do nothing on a non-numeric pane count instead of printing usage
issues.body:
## What happened

`tsl abc "cmd"` exits silently having done nothing — no panes, no usage message, no error. The same applies to `tsl 0` and `tsl -3`, and to `hsl` in `default/bash/fns/herdr`.

## Cause

In `default/bash/fns/tmux`, `tsl()` never validates its first argument:

```bash
local count="$1"
...
while (( ${#panes[@]} < count )); do
```

In bash arithmetic a non-numeric string is resolved as a *variable name*; an undefined one evaluates to `0`, so the loop condition `1 < 0` is false and the function falls straight through to sending the command to the single existing pane.

There is a smaller second-order surprise: because bash resolves the value recursively, a pane count that happens to name an existing shell variable takes that variable's value. With `x=50` set, `tsl x "cmd"` creates 50 panes.

I want to be precise that this is a robustness/UX issue rather than a runaway loop — a bare typo is harmless, just silent.

## What was expected

A non-numeric or non-positive pane count prints usage and returns 1, as the other argument errors in the same file do.

## Fix

```bash
if ! [[ $count =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Pane count must be a positive number, got: $count"
  return 1
fi
```

## System

- Omarchy 4.0.1-1
- `/usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/fns/tmux`, lines 5 and 14
- `/usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/fns/herdr` (`hsl`) has the same unchecked loop

issues.title: `omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation` drops `BROWSER`: first-agent OAuth browser runs in the terminal's process tree and aborts with SIGTRAP
issues.body:
### System details

AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, Radeon Graphics (Granite Ridge, `amdgpu`), Omarchy 4.0.1-1, Chromium 151.0.7922.173-1, Hyprland 0.56.2-1, uwsm 0.26.7-1, bash 5.3.15-1, kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2. Fresh install, first login.

### What's wrong?

**The defect**

`omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation:13` runs its payload under a non-interactive shell:

```bash
exec setsid uwsm-app -- xdg-terminal-exec --app-id=org.omarchy.terminal --title=Omarchy -e bash -c "$presentation_script"
```

`bash -c` is non-interactive, so `~/.bashrc` returns at its `[[ $- != *i* ]] && return` guard (line 5) and `default/bash/envs` is never sourced. `OMARCHY_PATH` and `EDITOR` survive because uwsm puts them in the session environment — but `BROWSER` does not, because it is deliberately shell-scoped only (`default/bash/envs:5-8`):

```bash
# Used by terminal programs (like gh) to open URLs detached from the terminal
# process tree. Shell-scoped on purpose: exporting BROWSER session-wide makes
# xdg-settings refuse to change the default browser.
export BROWSER="${BROWSER:-omarchy-launch-browser}"
```

Verified on 4.0.1:

```
$ bash -c  'echo "${BROWSER:-UNSET}"'   →  UNSET
$ bash -ic 'echo "${BROWSER:-UNSET}"'   →  omarchy-launch-browser
```

So every command run through the presentation terminal opens URLs with the browser attached to the terminal's process tree — precisely what that export exists to prevent.

**What it caused**

First login → "Set your default agent" → Claude Code:

```
11:03:59  xdg-terminal-exec ... -e bash -c 'omarchy-show-logo; omarchy-default-agent --install claude; ...'
11:04:25  chromium <claude.com OAuth authorize URL>          ← spawned by the agent, not detached
11:06:11  ~/.claude/.credentials.json written                ← login itself succeeds
11:07:35  Hyprland: failed to read client connection (pid 5782)
11:07:36.003  chromium FATAL
11:07:36  terminal scope ends (3min 36s)
```

`omarchy-default-agent --install` ends in `exec omarchy-agent --inline`, so the agent *is* the terminal. When login finishes and it exits, the terminal goes — and takes the browser's child processes with it.

Chromium's fatal, recovered from the core:

```
[6326:6326:0829/110736.003148:FATAL:content/browser/gpu/gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

Symbolized stack (Arch debuginfod):

```
logging::LogMessage::Flush()
logging::LogMessageFatal::~LogMessageFatal()
content::(anonymous namespace)::IntentionallyCrashBrowserForUnusableGpuProcess()
content::GpuDataManagerImplPrivate::FallBackToNextGpuMode()
content::GpuDataManagerImpl::FallBackToNextGpuModeDueToCrash()
content::GpuProcessHost::RecordProcessCrash()
content::GpuProcessHost::OnProcessLaunchFailed(int)
content::BrowserChildProcessHostImpl::OnProcessLaunchFailed(int)
content::ChildProcessLauncher::Notify(...)
content::internal::ChildProcessLauncherHelper::PostLaunchOnClientThread(...)
base::TaskAnnotator::RunTaskImpl(base::PendingTask&)
... base::MessagePumpGlib::Run ... content::BrowserMain ... ChromeMain
```

`SIGTRAP` with `si_code=SI_KERNEL` is Chromium's `int3` self-abort, not a fault. Chromium tried to **launch** a GPU process, the launch failed, no GPU fallback mode was left, and it takes the browser down by design.

That it was not launched detached is confirmed by cgroup: PID 6326 had only Chromium's self-created `app-org.chromium.Chromium-6326.scope`. A normally-launched Chromium also carries an `app-Hyprland-chromium-*.scope`, and at 11:04:25 there was no `uwsm_app-daemon` request and no `omarchy-browser-*` unit.

Ruled out: OOM (84 GiB free, no oomd or kernel kills), task limits (633 of 112847), `amdgpu` (clean init, completely silent 11:06–11:08), the bundled Chromium extensions (renderer-side, absent from the stack), and the 11:03 upgrades (`archlinux-keyring`, `aether`, `mise-bin`).

**Proven vs inferred.** The abort path, the missing `BROWSER`, and the un-detached launch are directly evidenced. That the terminal's teardown is what made the GPU relaunch fail is inferred from the sub-second coincidence — the kill signal is not recoverable after the fact. The missing `BROWSER` is a defect on its own terms regardless, since it defeats the stated purpose of that export.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh Omarchy 4.0.1 install, first login.
2. "Set your default agent" → Claude Code (any agent that signs in through a browser).
3. Complete the OAuth login in the Chromium window that opens.
4. Let the agent exit / the setup terminal close.

Chromium aborts; `coredumpctl` records a `SIGTRAP`.

### Related

- **#7174** hits the identical fatal (`gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417`, same message) in the identical first-agent flow, but sets it aside as "a Chromium/Mesa abort, not this stacking bug". It is not Mesa — it is this. That issue is about window stacking; this is the crash it scoped out. It also records that Grok launches via `uwsm-app -- /usr/bin/chromium`, i.e. each agent improvises its own browser launch exactly because `BROWSER` is absent.
- **#8394** is a *different* SIGTRAP: early startup, single-threaded `ChromeMain` stack, before content loads. Not this one.

### Proposed fix

Source Omarchy's own env file at the head of the presentation script:

```diff
-presentation_script="omarchy-show-logo; $cmd; if (( \$? != 130 )); then omarchy-show-done; fi"
+presentation_script="source \"\${OMARCHY_PATH:-/usr/share/omarchy}/default/bash/envs\"; omarchy-show-logo; $cmd; if (( \$? != 130 )); then omarchy-show-done; fi"
```

Verified on 4.0.1:

- restores `BROWSER=omarchy-launch-browser`
- still works with `OMARCHY_PATH` unset (falls back to `/usr/share/omarchy`)
- emits nothing on stdout/stderr and exits 0, so the presentation is unchanged

It keeps `BROWSER` shell-scoped — no session-wide export, so `xdg-settings` still behaves — and fixes all seven callers of the wrapper at once (`omarchy-menu.jsonc`, `Panel.qml`, `SystemUpdate.qml`, `install-voxtype.hook`, `setup-fingerprint.hook`, `transcode.py`, `wifi.sh`).

---

Filed by Claude Opus 5 via Claude Code.

issues.title: omarchy update wedged by unowned kernel-modules-hook leftovers after release-migration kernel downgrade
issues.body:
## System details

- Omarchy: 4.0.1 (was 4.0.0 when the bug hit; arrived there via the omarchy-dev → 4.0.0 release migration)
- CPU: 13th Gen Intel Core i5-1335U (ThinkPad E16)
- GPU: Intel Raptor Lake-P Iris Xe
- kernel-modules-hook 0.1.7-3 (installed via `omarchy-base.packages`)

## What happened

`omarchy update` aborted with **6,454** raw pacman errors, all of the form:

```
error: failed to commit transaction (conflicting files)
linux: /usr/lib/modules/7.1.9-arch1-2/... exists in filesystem
```

Every conflicting path was inside `/usr/lib/modules/7.1.9-arch1-2/`, which existed on disk but was owned by no package. The update died before any transaction started, with no guidance beyond the generic "Something went wrong during the update!" trap message.

## Root cause

This is an interaction between the release migration's kernel **downgrade** and `kernel-modules-hook` (which Omarchy installs in the base package set):

1. Machine was on the omarchy-dev channel with `linux 7.1.9.arch1-2` installed **and booted**.
2. The omarchy-dev → 4.0.0 release migration synced back to the stable repo state, which at that moment meant `downgraded linux (7.1.9.arch1-2 -> 7.1.8.arch1-3)` (from `pacman.log`).
3. kernel-modules-hook did its job: its `10-linux-modules-post` hook rsync'd the *running* kernel's (7.1.9) modules back into `/usr/lib/modules/` so the live system kept working — leaving the whole 7.1.9 tree **unowned by any package**.
4. The user (me) didn't reboot.
5. Arch later re-released `linux 7.1.9.arch1-2`. The next `omarchy update` tries to upgrade 7.1.8 → 7.1.9 and pacman refuses: every package file collides with the unowned hook-restored copy.

Two properties make this a persistent wedge rather than a self-healing hiccup:

- pacman's file-conflict check runs **before** PreTransaction hooks, so `10-linux-modules-pre` never gets a chance to move the directory out of the way.
- kernel-modules-hook's `linux-modules-cleanup.service` explicitly **skips the running kernel's tree**, so as long as you stay booted into 7.1.9, nothing ever cleans it up, and every `omarchy update` fails the same way. (`omarchy update` only passes `--overwrite '/usr/share/omarchy/*'`, which doesn't cover it.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Be booted into kernel version X with kernel-modules-hook installed.
2. Downgrade `linux` to an older version (the dev → 4.0.0 release migration did this implicitly) — the hook restores X's modules as unowned files.
3. Without rebooting, wait for the repo to offer version X again and run `omarchy update`.
4. Update fails with thousands of "exists in filesystem" conflicts.

## Expected

Either the update handles the conflict (the on-disk files are byte-identical to the package's — I verified with `diff -rq` against the cached `linux-7.1.9.arch1-2` package before overwriting), or the failure message tells the user what's going on instead of dumping ~6,500 raw pacman lines.

## Workarounds that fix it

- `sudo pacman -S linux --overwrite '/usr/lib/modules/<running-kver>/*'`, then rerun `omarchy update` (what I did — clean result, package took ownership of identical files), or
- reboot first (into the installed older kernel), which lets `linux-modules-cleanup.service` sweep the now-not-running unowned tree, then update.

## Suggested fix

In `omarchy-update-system-pkgs`, when the upgrade fails and the conflicts are confined to `/usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/` with that directory unowned (`pacman -Qo` fails) and the `linux` upgrade target matches the running kernel version, retry with `--overwrite "/usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/*"` — or at minimum detect the pattern and print "reboot, then update again" instead of the raw pacman spew. Could also be handled in the migration that performs the downgrade.

Happy to PR the detection/retry if you'd take it.

issues.title: omarchy-network-speedtest: samples divided by a nominal 1s that is never measured
issues.body:
### What's wrong?

`omarchy-network-speedtest` divides each sample by a nominal 1.0 seconds that it
never measures, so every reported sample is inflated, and a constant link rate is
reported as a varying one.

The sampling loop:

```bash
while any_alive; do
  sleep 1
  rx_after=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/statistics/rx_bytes")
  tx_after=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/statistics/tx_bytes")
  rate=$(awk ... 'BEGIN { print (after - before) * 8 / 1000000 }')
  format_mbps "$rate"
  rx_before=$rx_after
  ...
done
```

The byte delta is divided by 1 second implicitly, but one iteration is `sleep 1`
plus two `cat` subshells and two `awk` subshells. The real interval is longer
than a second, so bytes accumulated over ~1.01s are attributed to exactly 1.00s.

### Steps to reproduce

Time the loop shape (no network required):

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  t0=$EPOCHREALTIME
  sleep 1
  cat /sys/class/net/lo/statistics/rx_bytes >/dev/null
  cat /sys/class/net/lo/statistics/tx_bytes >/dev/null
  awk 'BEGIN{ print (100-50)*8/1000000 }' >/dev/null
  awk -v v=1 'BEGIN{ printf "%.0f\n", v }' >/dev/null
  awk -v a="$t0" -v b="$EPOCHREALTIME" 'BEGIN{ printf "%.4f\n", b-a }'
done
```

### Actual result

Ten iterations: mean **1.0103 s**, min 1.0094, max 1.0117. Every sample is
therefore reported about **1.03% high**.

Because the overhead varies per iteration, the error is not a constant offset.
Feeding a link with a genuinely constant 984 Mbps of counted bytes:

| | Reported Mbps |
|---|---|
| Current (divide by nominal 1.0s) | 992.4, 992.6, 992.7, 992.8, 992.8, 993.6, 994.3, 994.5 |
| Divide by measured elapsed | 984.0 x 8 |

So the loop manufactures jitter that is not present on the link. This matters
for any consumer that aggregates the sample stream: a consumer that takes the
peak sample systematically selects the iteration with the largest timing error,
which can push a reported figure above the interface's negotiated line rate.

### Expected result

Reported throughput reflects bytes divided by the interval actually elapsed.

### Suggested fix

`$EPOCHREALTIME` is a bash builtin, so this adds no subprocess:

```bash
while any_alive; do
  t0=$EPOCHREALTIME
  sleep 1
  rx_after=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/statistics/rx_bytes")
  tx_after=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/statistics/tx_bytes")
  elapsed=$(awk -v a="$t0" -v b="$EPOCHREALTIME" 'BEGIN{ print (b - a) }')
  rate=$(awk -v before="$rx_before" -v after="$rx_after" -v el="$elapsed" 'BEGIN {
    if (after < before || el <= 0) print 0
    else print (after - before) * 8 / 1000000 / el
  }')
  ...
done
```

### Scope

This is only about the sampling interval. The separate problem of selecting the
interface the transfer actually uses is already reported in #7551, and this
change is independent of it.

### System details

Omarchy 4.0.1-1, bash 5.3.15. The defect is in shell arithmetic and is not
hardware or network dependent.

issues.title: Keyboard input dead on the focused window after a long idle lock, workspace switch restores it
issues.body:
### What's wrong?

After a long idle, I unlock and no window on the workspace takes keyboard input.

The window still looks focused. It keeps its focus border, the bar still names it, and `hyprctl activewindow` still reports it. But nothing I type reaches any client. Compositor keybinds still work, so the keyboard is fine.

Any workspace or window switch brings input back. `SUPER+2` then `SUPER+1` fixes it instantly. So does `SUPER+left/right`.

It doesn't happen on a short lock.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Focus a terminal on workspace 1 and leave the machine alone.
2. Let the screensaver (150s) and then the lock (300s) kick in.
3. Leave it locked at least 10 minutes.
4. Wake the display and unlock.
5. Try to type. Nothing lands.
6. Press `SUPER+2`, then `SUPER+1`. Typing works again.

### What I'd expect

After unlocking, the window Hyprland reports as active should hold keyboard focus. No manual workspace switch needed.

### System details

- Omarchy `4.0.1-1`, Hyprland `0.56.2-1`, quickshell `0.3.1-1`, kernel `7.1.8-arch1-3`
- Intel i9-9900K, NVIDIA RTX 4070, `nvidia-open-dkms` and `nvidia-utils` `610.57.04-1`
- Single monitor, LG UltraGear on `HDMI-A-1`, 3840x2160@119.88, scale 2
- Terminal is `foot`. Stock idle config: `{ "screensaver": 150, "lock": 300 }`
- No suspend involved. Machine was up 3 days straight across all of this.

### What the socket shows

I caught one with a capture running. Lock at 12:43:10, unlock at 12:56:23, so 13m13s. From `.socket2.sock`:

```
12:56:14 monitorremoved>>HDMI-A-1
12:56:14 focusedmon>>FALLBACK,4
12:56:14 monitoradded>>FALLBACK
12:56:14 activewindow>>,                <-- focus cleared
12:56:17 monitoradded>>HDMI-A-1
12:56:17 focusedmon>>HDMI-A-1,1
12:56:17 monitorremoved>>FALLBACK
                                        <-- no activewindow event, focus never comes back
12:56:23 (unlocked)
12:56:30 activewindow>>foot,...         <-- only after I switched windows by hand
```

The monitor drops out. Everything migrates to `FALLBACK` and Hyprland clears focus. The real monitor is back 3 seconds later. Focus is never restored. There's no `activewindow` event between `12:56:17` and my manual switch at `12:56:30`.

This `hyprctl` dump is from `12:56:24`, one second after the unlock, before I touched anything:

```
--- activewindow ---
{ "address": "0x5570ff79c070", "class": "foot", "workspace": { "id": 1, "name": "1" },
  "mapped": true, "visible": true, "acceptsInput": true, "focusHistoryID": 0, ... }
--- activeworkspace ---
{"id":1,"name":"1","lastwindow":"0x5570ff79c070"}
--- layers (overlay) ---
[{"mon":"HDMI-A-1","overlay":[]}]
```

So `hyprctl` names a window with `focusHistoryID: 0` and `acceptsInput: true`. The event stream says focus was cleared and never restored. That mismatch is the visible bug: the window keeps its border, the bar keeps its name, and no client gets a key. The overlay level is empty, so no stray layer is holding input.

The workspace disagrees too. The stream emits `workspace>>6` at `12:56:17`, the dump at `12:56:24` reports workspace `1`.

### How often

On wake from a long lock, `omarchy-shell` logs a full loss of outputs while still locked:

```
2026-08-30T12:56:14 kernel: nvidia-modeset: WARNING: GPU:0: HDMI FRL link training failed.
2026-08-30T12:56:14 omarchy-shell:  INFO qt.qpa.wayland: There are no outputs - creating placeholder screen
2026-08-30T12:56:18 omarchy-shell:  WARN quickshell.hyprland.ipc: Got removal for monitor "FALLBACK" which was not previously tracked.
2026-08-30T12:56:23 omarchy-shell: DEBUG qml: omarchy lock ... unlocked
```

There are 15 of these clusters this boot. 14 land seconds before an unlock. The odd one out is a wake I didn't unlock.

| Lock duration | Output dropped before unlock? |
| --- | --- |
| 5s, 8s, 14s, 19s, 1m48s | No (5/5) |
| 9m06s, 9m51s, 11m, 13m13s, 14m30s, 19m16s, 19m50s, 1h01m, 1h38m, 2h14m, 2h38m, 4h32m, 16h49m, 39h20m | Yes (14/14) |

Every lock over 9 minutes dropped the output. None of the five under 2 minutes did. I've got nothing between 2 and 9 minutes, so I don't know where the line sits.

One caveat on that table. It tracks output loss, read from the journal afterwards. It isn't a record of input dying. I only saw dead input on the times I came back and tried to type. The 13m13s row is the one with the trace above.

13 of the 15 clusters land on the same second as the `FRL link training failed` warning. Two don't, so that warning travels with these wakes but isn't required.

I couldn't force it on a short timescale. 80 seconds of `hl.dsp.dpms({ action = "disable" })` never dropped the output, and focus was fine after. I haven't tried a longer forced one.

### Upstream

Hyprland [discussion #15554](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/discussions/15554) is the same thing on a sole monitor. Same `FALLBACK` round trip, same `activewindow>>,`, same workspace switch to recover. It was closed with a Lua workaround after this reply:

> I don't think we enforce focus on monitor addition to not disrupt current state. With lua I think the workaround is totally reasonable

Reading that, I don't expect a fix upstream. Omarchy's idle lock is what puts the display into the state that leads to the round trip, so this felt like the right place to raise it.

One thing worth flagging: focus is already gone at `12:56:14`, before I authenticate. The unlock isn't losing it. It hands back a session that already has nothing focused. Whether the lock matters at all, I haven't tested.

Possibly related, same `FALLBACK` and output loss pattern: #7811 (similar dead keyboard input after lid-open resume), #7380 (shell crashes on `FALLBACK` removal at wake, mine survives), #8580 and #8946 (monitors dropping HPD after DPMS off).

### Happy to help

Could I put a PR together for this? I was thinking a `monitor.added` handler that re-asserts focus when a `FALLBACK` migration just happened, along the lines of the Lua workaround above. Happy to go another way if you'd rather 🤔

issues.title: [hyprland] Steam main window defaults to small floating 1100x700 instead of tiled/maximizable
issues.body:
### Summary
In Omarchy 4, the default Hyprland window rules force the main Steam client window to float at a fixed size of `1100x700`, while `suppress_event = "maximize"` is globally configured in `windows.lua`. This causes Steam's main store/library window to feel cramped on high-DPI/larger displays, and clicking the CSD maximize button inside the Steam client fails to maximize the window.

### Current Implementation
In `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/apps/steam.lua`:
```lua
o.window("steam", { float = true, idle_inhibit = "fullscreen" })
o.window({ class = "steam", title = "Steam" }, { center = true, size = { 1100, 700 } })
```

And in `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/windows.lua`:
```lua
o.window(".*", { suppress_event = "maximize" })
```

### Problem
Because Steam runs under XWayland with custom Client-Side Decorations (CSD), clicking the maximize button within Steam's title bar does nothing, and the initial 1100x700 geometry leaves the store and library narrow with large black borders unless the user manually invokes `SUPER + F` or overrides the rule in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`.

### Proposed Solution
Allow the main Steam client (`title = "^Steam$"`) to default to tiled mode (`tile = true`) or provide an easy toggle, while keeping auxiliary popups and the Friends List floating:

```lua
o.window("steam", { float = true, idle_inhibit = "fullscreen" })
o.window({ class = "steam", title = "^Steam$" }, { tile = true })
o.window({ class = "steam", title = "Friends List" }, { size = { 460, 800 }, float = true })
```

issues.title: Update > Hardware > Trackpad silently no-ops on Apple bcm5974 trackpads
issues.body:
## What happened

On a 2011 MacBook Pro, selecting **Super menu → Update → Hardware → Trackpad** opens a floating terminal that immediately disappears without displaying or doing anything.

This menu entry looks like a trackpad control/settings item, but it invokes:

```text
omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation omarchy-restart-trackpad
```

Running the underlying command directly confirms the silent success:

```console
$ omarchy-restart-trackpad
$ echo $?
0
```

The trackpad is unchanged.

## Root cause

`omarchy-restart-trackpad` only handles:

1. devices under `/sys/bus/i2c/drivers/i2c_hid_acpi/i2c-*`
2. the `intel_quicki2c` module

This MacBook's correctly detected internal trackpad is USB and uses the `bcm5974` driver:

```text
Hyprland device name: bcm5974
ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD=1
ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION=internal
ID_MODEL=Apple_Internal_Keyboard___Trackpad
ID_MODEL_ID=0246
ID_USB_DRIVER=bcm5974
```

There are no matching `i2c_hid_acpi` devices and `intel_quicki2c` is not loaded. Both branches are therefore skipped, the script prints nothing, and exits 0. Because the menu entry is displayed unconditionally, it presents a dead action on this hardware.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Boot Omarchy on a MacBook using the `bcm5974` trackpad driver.
2. Open the Super menu.
3. Select **Update → Hardware → Trackpad**.
4. Observe the floating terminal disappear immediately and the trackpad remain unchanged.
5. Run `omarchy-restart-trackpad` directly; it produces no output and exits 0.

## Expected behavior

One of:

- support resetting the detected `bcm5974` device safely;
- hide the recovery action when none of its supported driver paths exists; or
- retain the action but report clearly that this trackpad driver is unsupported and return a non-zero status.

## System details

- Omarchy: 4.0.2-1
- Kernel: 7.1.9-arch1-2
- Hardware: 2011 15-inch MacBook Pro
- Trackpad: Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad, USB ID `05ac:0246`
- Driver: `bcm5974`

## Related but distinct

#9190 covers `omarchy-hw-touchpad` failing to recognize the name `bcm5974`, which hides/breaks the touchpad enable/disable toggle. Fixing that detector does not fix this issue: the separately exposed `omarchy-restart-trackpad` action still only implements I2C/Intel reset paths.

issues.title: hyprland.lua loads nwg-displays monitors.lua but not workspaces.lua, so workspace-to-monitor assignments never apply
issues.body:
## System details

```text
Omarchy: 4.0.1-1
Kernel: 6.18.46-1-lts
Hyprland: 0.56.2
CPU: 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900K
GPU: NVIDIA RTX A4500 (dual)
nwg-displays: 0.4.3-1
Monitors: DP-1 LG Ultra HD, DP-2 LG SDQHD, DP-3 LG SDQHD
hyprctl configerrors: clean
hyprctl plugin list: no plugins loaded
```

## What's wrong?

The default `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` loads `hypr.monitors` but not `hypr.workspaces`:

```lua
require("hypr.monitors")
require("hypr.input")
require("hypr.bindings")
require("hypr.looknfeel")
require("hypr.autostart")
```

nwg-displays (0.4.3, the stock Arch package) writes **both** files when you save a display layout: `monitors.lua` via `hl.monitor({...})` and `workspaces.lua` via `hl.workspace_rule({...})`. Both `.lua` paths are derived from the `.conf` path in the nwg-displays source (`nwg_displays/main.py` around line 905/937 for workspaces, `nwg_displays/settings_applier/settings_applier.py` around line 116/121 for monitors).

Because `hyprland.lua` requires only `hypr.monitors`, the monitor geometry applies but the workspace-to-monitor rules in `workspaces.lua` are never loaded. Workspaces then fall back to Hyprland's default placement, so the assignments set in nwg-displays silently do nothing. `hyprctl configerrors` stays clean, because the file is simply never required (not a parse error).

The same omission is present on the current `quattro` branch template (`config/hypr/hyprland.lua`), which requires `hypr.monitors` but not `hypr.workspaces`, and ships a `monitors.lua` template but no `workspaces.lua`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In nwg-displays, assign specific workspaces to specific monitors (for example ws 1 and 5 to DP-1, ws 2 and 6 to DP-2, ws 3 and 7 to DP-3) and Apply.
2. nwg-displays writes `~/.config/hypr/workspaces.lua` with `hl.workspace_rule({...})` entries (and `monitors.lua`).
3. `hyprctl reload`, or reboot.

## Actual result

Workspace-to-monitor assignments do not apply. With a rule binding workspace 5 to DP-1, workspace 5 opens on a different monitor. Monitor geometry from the same nwg-displays run is correct, because `monitors.lua` is required.

## Expected result

Workspaces open on the monitors assigned in nwg-displays, matching the `hl.workspace_rule` entries in `workspaces.lua`, consistent with how `monitors.lua` is already honored.

## Workaround

Add one line to `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`:

```lua
require("hypr.monitors")
require("hypr.workspaces")
require("hypr.input")
```

After `hyprctl reload` the rules load and `configerrors` stays clean. Workspaces already created on the wrong monitor need to be moved once (or a fresh login), since workspace rules apply at creation time.

## Suggested fix

Load `hypr.workspaces` from the default `hyprland.lua`, guarded so it is a no-op when the file is absent (a fresh install has no `workspaces.lua`), for example via the existing `require_optional` helper already used for the theme in `default/hypr/omarchy.lua`. That way users who set workspace assignments in nwg-displays get them honored, and fresh installs are unaffected.

issues.title: Quickshell SIGSEGV in QFactoryLoader::metaDataKeys after hibernate resume when opening omarchy-menu
issues.body:
## What happened

The Omarchy shell (`quickshell -n -p /usr/share/omarchy/shell`) SIGSEGV'd 15 seconds after resume from hibernate, while opening `omarchy-menu`. Quickshell's crash handler caught the fault and re-raised it (`si_code: SI_TKILL`). The shell auto-restarted; no user data was lost.

This is a one-off of this stack on this machine. Earlier local quickshell dumps are a different karaoke `IdleInhibitor` destructor and a session-lock abort.

## Expected

Opening the Omarchy menu after hibernate resume should load app icons without killing the shell.

## Steps to reproduce

Not confirmed as 100% reliable (this stack has happened once here), but the timeline is tight:

1. Hibernate the machine (this session slept ~14h).
2. Resume.
3. Within ~15 seconds, open the Omarchy menu.
4. Shell dies in `QQuickPixmapReader` while decoding an app icon.

On this machine the job in flight was:

```
/usr/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/one.alynx.showmethekey.svg
```

(`showmethekey 1.21.0-1`). The file is a normal intact SVG; the crash is not a corrupt icon.

## Stack (symbolized)

Crashing thread is Qt's `QQuickPixmapReader`. The original fault is `QIODevice::read(this=0x1)` — a garbage device pointer, not a typical heap UAF address — while `QFactoryLoader` parses **static plugin** CBOR metadata to satisfy `QImageReader::imageCount()`.

```
#3  qs::crash::signalHandler (sig=11) at quickshell/src/crash/handler.cpp:93
#4  <signal handler called>
#5–#8  QIODevice::read (this=0x1, maxSize=46)   at qtbase/src/corelib/io/qiodevice.cpp:1003
#9–#14 QCborStreamReader::readAllString()      at qtbase/src/corelib/serialization/qcborstreamreader.cpp
#15–#18 iterateInPluginMetaData / QFactoryLoaderMetaDataKeysExtractor
#19 QFactoryLoader::metaDataKeys()             at qtbase/src/corelib/plugin/qfactoryloader.cpp:537
#20 QFactoryLoader::keyMap()                   at qtbase/src/corelib/plugin/qfactoryloader.cpp:596
#23 QImageReader::imageCount() const
#24 readImage(...)                             at qtdeclarative/.../qquickpixmapcache.cpp:512
#25 QQuickPixmapReader::processJob (...)
        localFile = "/usr/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/one.alynx.showmethekey.svg"
#26 QQuickPixmapReader::processJobs
#41 QQuickPixmapReader::run
```

The systemd-coredump contains only this LWP (the pixmap-reader thread). Other in-flight work is not in the dump.

Last Quickshell log line before the crash:

```
DEBUG quickshell.hyprland.ipc.events: Received event: "openlayer>>omarchy-menu"
```

`plugins/menu/Menu.qml` loads those icons with a normal `Image { asynchronous: true; source: appLibrary.iconSource(...) }`.

## What this is / is not

**Proved:** the SIGSEGV is inside Qt 6.11.2 (`QFactoryLoader` / `QCborStreamReader`), hosted by Omarchy's bundled shell, triggered by menu icon decode after hibernate resume.

**Not proved:** whether hibernate left plugin-metadata state corrupt, or the menu's burst of icon loads just hit a latent Qt bug. The dump cannot distinguish those.

Not the same as:

- #7098 — omarchy-menu crash, but QML JIT while typing
- #8026 — same `QQuickPixmapReader` thread, but OpenSSL while loading HTTPS album art

The immediate fault is in Qt; the user-facing trigger is Omarchy's shell/menu. Filing here because this is the Omarchy-shipped Quickshell config (`/usr/share/omarchy/shell`).

## System details

- `omarchy version`: 4.0.2-1
- Kernel: 7.1.9-arch1-2
- Hyprland 0.56.2-1
- quickshell 0.3.1-1
- qt6-base 6.11.2-2, qt6-declarative 6.11.2-1, qt6-svg 6.11.2-1, qt6-imageformats 6.11.2-1
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (amdgpu, Navi 48), MODE1 reset on this resume
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X
- Desktop: Gigabyte X570 AORUS MASTER, Wayland / Hyprland, 3840x2160

`omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print` was run at 2026-09-01 10:56 EEST and wrote `/tmp/omarchy-debug.log` (113 KiB). Relevant excerpt:

```

Kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2 x86_64
```

issues.title: Low-battery warning storm: notification every ~3s when AC online status flaps (latch resets on onBatteryChanged)
issues.body:
## What happened

While my laptop was sitting at the lock screen discharging through the low-battery range, the shell sent **"Time to recharge!" every ~3.2 seconds, continuously, for 14 minutes** — ~260 critical notifications between 14:11 and 14:25 (10% down to 3%), until the machine died.

Notification state files (one per popup, timestamped) show the cadence:

```
14:11:45 +  0.0s Time to recharge! | Battery is down to 10%
14:11:50 +  4.2s Time to recharge! | Battery is down to 10%
14:11:53 +  3.3s Time to recharge! | Battery is down to 10%
...continues every ~3.2s through 10% → 9% → 8% → ... → 3%...
14:25:29 +  3.0s Time to recharge! | Battery is down to 3%
```

## Root cause

The journal shows the AC adapter's reported online status was **flapping every ~3.2 seconds** during the same window (UCSI/PD trouble at critical charge — `ucsi_acpi USBC000:00: unknown error 256`). The ACAD udev events alternate between the plugged and unplugged rules at that cadence:

```
14:11:52 (udev-worker): ACAD: ... omarchy-wifi-powersave off' failed with exit code 1.
14:11:52 (udev-worker): ACAD: ... omarchy-wifi-powersave on' failed with exit code 1.
14:11:53 kernel: ucsi_acpi USBC000:00: unknown error 256
14:11:55 (udev-worker): ACAD: ... omarchy-wifi-powersave off' ...
14:11:55 (udev-worker): ACAD: ... omarchy-wifi-powersave on' ...
```

In `shell/plugins/services/battery/BatteryModel.js`, the notified-latch is recomputed as `notifiedLowBattery: low` on every check:

```js
var low = isDischarging(device, onBattery, dischargingState) && level <= threshold
return { level: level, notify: low && !alreadyNotified, notifiedLowBattery: low }
```

and `Service.qml` calls `checkBattery()` from `onOnBatteryChanged`. So every flap runs two checks: the "on AC" one computes `low = false` and **resets the latch**, and the "on battery" one immediately re-notifies. One critical notification per flap cycle, forever.

Since critical popups never auto-expire (#9361), all ~260 piled up on screen until the battery died. Each flap also re-ran `omarchy-powerprofiles-set` (visible as `omarchy-power-profile.service` start/stop churn every ~3s).

## Expected

One warning per low-battery episode. A momentary blip in `onBattery` / device state should not re-arm the warning.

## Suggested fix

Any (or all) of:
- **Hysteresis on the latch:** only clear `notifiedLowBattery` once the battery is genuinely recovering (level > threshold, or charging state sustained for e.g. 30s) — not on any instant where `low` computes false.
- **Rate-limit** `sendLowBatteryWarning` (e.g. at most once per 5 minutes).
- Pass a **replaces-id** (`-r`) from `omarchy-battery-low` so repeats coalesce into a single popup instead of stacking.

## System

- Framework Laptop 13 (AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS / Radeon 780M)
- Omarchy `4.0.0.r1846.g946704f-1`, quickshell `0.3.1-1`, kernel `7.1.9-arch1-2`

Related: #9361 (critical toasts never expire — the aggravator that made this a wall of popups), #8813 (low-battery toast persists after charger connect).

issues.title: Screenshots take ~1.6s on 6K: grim uses default PNG compression (-l 6)
issues.body:
### What happened

`omarchy capture screenshot` takes **~1.6 seconds** to save a full-screen capture on a 6K display. The delay is not the screen capture — it is `grim` running at its default PNG compression level (6).

`omarchy-capture-screenshot` invokes `grim` with no `-l` flag in all three code paths:

```
65:    grim -g "$SELECTION" "$FILEPATH" || exit 1
76:    grim -g "$SELECTION" - | wl-copy --type image/png
79:    grim -g "$SELECTION" "$FILEPATH" || exit 1
```

grim(1) defaults to `-l 6`. At 6144x3456 (21.2 MPix) zlib dominates total runtime.

### Measurements

Display: LG UltraFine 6K, `6144x3456@60.02Hz`, scale 2. 3 runs each, median:

| Command | Time | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `grim -t ppm` (capture only, no encode) | **127 ms** | 61 MB |
| `grim -l 1` | **564 ms** | 8.2 MB |
| `grim -l 4` | 746 ms | 6.9 MB |
| `grim` (current behaviour, `-l 6`) | **1628 ms** | 6.4 MB |

Capture costs 127 ms. The remaining ~1500 ms is PNG compression. `-l 1` is **2.9x faster** for ~28% more bytes.

The effect scales with pixel count, so it is proportionally milder at 1080p but still present:

| 1920x1080 region | Time | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `grim -l 6` | 495 ms | 1.8 MB |
| `grim -l 1` | 223 ms | 2.3 MB |

### Expected

A screenshot should feel immediate. Spending ~1.5 s of CPU to save ~1.8 MB is a poor trade for a transient screenshot, especially on the HiDPI displays where Omarchy is most likely to be used.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Attach a 4K or higher display.
2. `time grim /tmp/a.png`
3. `time grim -l 1 /tmp/b.png`
4. Compare. The gap widens with resolution.

### Suggested fix

Pass a lower compression level in `omarchy-capture-screenshot`:

```diff
-    grim -g "$SELECTION" "$FILEPATH" || exit 1
+    grim -l 1 -g "$SELECTION" "$FILEPATH" || exit 1
```

`-l 1` gives the largest win; `-l 4` is a middle ground (746 ms, 6.9 MB) if file size matters more. Applying it to the `wl-copy` path matters most, since a clipboard image is discarded almost immediately and its compression ratio is irrelevant.

### Unrelated note

`omarchy-capture-region` uses a fixed `sleep .1` after starting the `hyprpicker` freeze. On this machine the hyprpicker layer registers in ~7 ms, so the 100 ms is mostly dead time. Minor next to the above, but it is on the same path.

### System

- Omarchy 4.0.2-1
- CPU: Intel Core 5 320
- GPU: Intel Wildcat Lake `[8086:fd80]` (xe)
- Hyprland 0.56.2
- grim 1.5.0-2
- Display: LG UltraFine 6K, 6144x3456@60, scale 2

issues.title: Display panel scale-preset button loses a border edge at 1.25x (not 1.6x)
issues.body:
## What happened

At display scale 1.25x specifically, the scale-preset buttons ("1x",
"1.25x", "1.6x", "2x", ...) in the Display panel (bar's Monitor widget)
lose a border on one edge — observed as the "1x" button's left border
missing.

Confirmed **not** reproducible at 1.6x or other non-integer scales tested —
only 1.25x. Since `cellWidth`'s fractional value (see root cause) doesn't
depend on the display scale at all, only on the panel's fixed logical
width, the scale factor only determines whether that fixed fractional
remainder happens to multiply out close enough to a whole device pixel to
vanish under anti-aliasing. That it reproduces at 1.25x but not 1.6x here
is consistent with that, but is empirical, not derived — worth checking
against other scales (1.5x, 1.75x, etc.) too.

## Expected

Every scale-preset button keeps its full border regardless of display
scale.

## Root cause

`plugins/panels/monitor/Panel.qml` (around line 768-788):

```qml
Grid {
  id: scaleRow
  width: parent.width
  columns: root.scaleValues.length
  spacing: Style.spacing.xs

  readonly property real cellWidth: root.scaleValues.length > 0
    ? (width - spacing * (columns - 1)) / columns
    : 0

  Repeater {
    model: root.scaleValues
    ScalePill {
      width: scaleRow.cellWidth
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

`cellWidth` is a raw, unrounded real-number division (e.g. with 6 presets,
`(280 - 15) / 6 = 44.1666...`). Everywhere else in the shell, sizes are
funneled through `Style.space(px)` (`Commons/Style.qml`), which explicitly
`Math.round()`s to a whole logical pixel — apparently for exactly this
reason. This one spot bypasses that convention, so each `ScalePill`'s
fractional width (and the fractional x-offsets it cascades across the row)
doesn't land on device-pixel boundaries once multiplied by a non-integer
display scale. The pill's 1px `Rectangle.border` then anti-aliases to
near-zero coverage on the affected edge.

At an integer scale this is invisible (logical-pixel-integer × integer
scale = integer device pixel regardless of the fractional cellWidth
underneath); at 1.25x/1.6x it isn't.

## Fix

Round `cellWidth` like the rest of the codebase does, e.g.:

```qml
readonly property real cellWidth: root.scaleValues.length > 0
  ? Math.floor((width - spacing * (columns - 1)) / columns)
  : 0
```

(`Math.floor` rather than `Math.round` so the row's total width never
exceeds `width` and wraps/overflows.) Verified locally via
`omarchy plugin clone omarchy.monitor` — fixes the missing border with no
other visible side effects.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set display scale to 1.25x.
2. Open the Display panel from the bar's Monitor widget.
3. Look at the scale-preset button row — the "1x" button is missing a
   border on its left edge.

Not reproducible at 1.6x, or other non-integer scales tested — see note
above.

## System

- Omarchy: 4.0.2-1
- Hyprland: 0.56.2
- Quickshell: 0.3.1
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 7500F

(`omarchy debug` isn't available as a command on this Omarchy version, so I
couldn't attach its generated log.)

issues.title: Emoji picker does not insert selected emoji
issues.body:
### System details

- Omarchy: 4.0.2-1
- Hyprland: 0.56.2
- Kernel: 7.1.9-arch1-2
- Session: Wayland / Hyprland
- GPU: Intel Kaby Lake-R GT2 (UHD Graphics 620)
- wl-clipboard: 2.3.0
- wtype: 0.4
- fcitx5: 5.1.21 (running)

### What's wrong?

The built-in Omarchy emoji picker opens normally, but selecting an emoji does not insert anything into the focused text field. The picker closes after selection, but no emoji appears.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Focus any text input.
2. Open the Omarchy emoji picker with `Super+Ctrl+E`.
3. Click any emoji.
4. Observe that the picker closes but the emoji is not inserted.

### Expected behavior

The selected emoji should be inserted into the previously focused text input.

### Investigation

The picker invokes `omarchy-menu-emoji-insert`, which currently does the following:

- Copies the emoji with `wl-copy --type text/plain ...`, targeting the regular Wayland `CLIPBOARD` selection.
- Sends `Shift+Insert` via `wtype`.

On Wayland/Linux, `Shift+Insert` uses the `PRIMARY` selection in common applications, not `CLIPBOARD`. This leaves the paste operation reading a different selection, so nothing is inserted. In the affected session, the regular clipboard and primary selection were also observed to contain different values.

The likely fix is either to copy with `wl-copy --primary` when using `Shift+Insert`, or to keep using the regular clipboard and send the equivalent regular-clipboard paste shortcut where appropriate.

This appears to be a reproducible issue in the packaged Omarchy implementation rather than a local configuration, font, or Fcitx issue.

issues.title: omarchy-shell SIGSEGV in QQuickItem::mapToScene while Qt synthesizes a context-menu event
issues.body:
## What happened

Omarchy's desktop shell (`quickshell -n -p /usr/share/omarchy/shell`) SIGSEGV'd while handling a mouse event that Qt turned into a context-menu event.

- Time: Fri 2026-09-04 18:09:44 WEST
- PID: 9071
- Signal: SIGSEGV (`si_code: SI_TKILL` is Quickshell's crash handler re-raising; the original fault is the frame under `<signal handler called>`)
- Config: `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/shell.qml`
- Quickshell crash report: `~/.cache/quickshell/crashes/yv2lnukt/report.txt`

The wrapper logged the crash and restarted the shell immediately. The bar came back. No user documents were lost.

This is the first recorded `quickshell` coredump on this machine. Not an OOM: ~9 Gi available, swap unused, no OOM kill.

## What was expected

A right-click (or the platform equivalent: two-finger click, mouse menu button) on a shell surface should open a context menu or be ignored. It should not take down the shell.

## Steps to reproduce

Not reproduced on demand. The stack is enough to name the path:

1. Shell is running (`omarchy-shell` / `quickshell -n -p /usr/share/omarchy/shell`).
2. A mouse event is delivered to a Quickshell window (bar or panel).
3. Qt synthesizes a `QContextMenuEvent` from that mouse event (`QWindowPrivate::maybeSynthesizeContextMenuEvent`).
4. While walking the item tree, `QQuickItem::mapToScene` segfaults.

Around the crash: the shell had been up ~2 minutes after a reboot that followed an `omarchy-dev` upgrade; an MX Master 3S had connected a minute earlier; a grok agent window was focused. That is context, not a demonstrated trigger.

First-party bar buttons accept right-click (`shell/Ui/WidgetButton.qml`). Several user plugins do too, including `quickshell.spotify` on the bar. Those plugins are in-process QML, so they can be in the item tree without appearing in the C++ stack. I am not pinning this on a plugin.

## Stack

Demangled from the libraries. File/line debuginfo was not applied.

```
#0  raise (libc)                                        # crash handler re-raise
#1  quickshell                                          # crash handler
#2  <signal handler called>
#3  QQuickItem::mapToScene(QPointF const&) const
#4  QQuickDeliveryAgentPrivate::contextMenuTargets(QQuickItem*, QContextMenuEvent const*) const
#5  QQuickDeliveryAgentPrivate::deliverContextMenuEvent(QContextMenuEvent*)

#9  QWindowPrivate::maybeSynthesizeContextMenuEvent(QMouseEvent*)

#12 QWindowSystemInterface::sendWindowSystemEvents(...)
...
#   QCoreApplication::exec()
```

The usual reading of this shape: `mapToScene` walked a QQuickItem that was already destroyed (or whose parent was). A right-click handler that rebuilds or unloads widgets, then Qt still delivering the synthesized context-menu event to the old item, matches. The coredump contained only the GUI thread.

None mention `mapToScene`, `contextMenuTargets`, or `maybeSynthesizeContextMenuEvent`. GitHub's issue search API returns 422 for this repo; this was a title grep, not `gh search`.

issues.title: Recursive plugin inotify + 150ms reload: git checkout / save storms take down the shell
issues.body:
### System details

Intel Core Ultra 5 225, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, Omarchy 4.0.2-1, Hyprland 0.56.2

### What's wrong?

`shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml` runs `inotifywait -m -r` on `~/.config/omarchy/plugins` (the whole tree, including each plugin's `.git`). `localPluginIdForPath` already ignores `/.git/` paths, but:

1. the kernel still watches every git object dir (omamail's `.git` here is ~22M / hundreds of directories)
2. **working-tree** writes (a `git checkout`, or an editor saving QML) still fire `localPluginChanged`
3. `shell.qml` reloads the **entire** plugin graph on a 150ms timer

On this seat an omamail `git checkout` / merge at 12:22 produced a burst of `Local plugin changed, reloading: omamail`, ShortcutHelp.qml incubation errors, a second Quickshell (`already running`), then `Exiting due to IPC request`. Combined with `omarchy-launch-shell` treating exit 0 as a deliberate stop (see follow-up), the bar / idle / screensaver stayed dead until a manual `omarchy restart shell` hours later.

Expected: `.git` (and `__pycache__` / `node_modules`) are not watched; a save storm coalesces to one reload per second or so, not a full QML teardown per file.

Suggested guardrails in tree:

- pass `inotifywait --exclude '/\.git(/|$)|/__pycache__(/|$)|/node_modules(/|$)'` (and ideally do not recurse into those dirs)
- raise `localPluginReloadTimer.interval` from 150ms to ~1000ms

`--exclude` only filters events, not watches; skipping `.git` in the watch list is better. We did that out of tree with a PATH wrapper around `inotifywait` for the plugins invocation only.

issues.title: Fingerprint unlock rejected on first attempt after resume (Goodix, race with sleep-lock inhibitor)
issues.body:
## What happened

The first fingerprint attempt after resuming from suspend (and the first
attempt right after a session starts) is reliably rejected. A second attempt
a couple of seconds later succeeds. This is consistent across multiple boots
today.

Journal evidence points to a race between `fprintd` and Omarchy's own
suspend/lock handling:

1. At suspend time, `fprintd` tries to install its own sleep-delay inhibitor
   and fails because Omarchy's `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` inhibitor
   ("Lock screen before suspend") already holds that slot:
   ```
   fprintd[...]: Failed to install a sleep delay inhibitor: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.login1.OperationInProgress: The operation inhibition has been requested for is already running
   ```
2. On resume, the first automatic verify from the Quickshell lock screen
   (`omarchy-lock-fingerprint` PAM service) fires before fprintd's view of
   the device has caught up, and fails:
   ```
   fprintd[...]: Device reported an error during verify: Cannot run while suspended.
   ```
3. That failed verify leaves the sensor claimed, so the follow-up release
   also fails, and the user's finger swipe is rejected:
   ```
   quickshell[...]: pam_fprintd(omarchy-lock-fingerprint:auth): ReleaseDevice failed: Release failed with error: The device is still busy with another operation, please try again later.
   ```

I also caught one worse episode where the sensor's own firmware
overheat-protection tripped (`Device disabled to prevent overheating`) and
something kept retrying the verify once a second for about 14 minutes
straight with no backoff, until the machine suspended again. That looks like
a symptom of the same underlying "verify fires before the device/claim state
is actually ready" issue, not real heat.

Full excerpt (representative lines from 3 separate boots today) attached.

## What was expected

Fingerprint unlock to work on the first attempt after resume, the same as
subsequent attempts later in the session.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enroll a fingerprint (`fprintd-enroll`) with the Quickshell lock screen
   wired up (`omarchy apply lock` / `omarchy setup security fingerprint`).
2. Suspend the laptop (lid close or `omarchy system lock` + suspend).
3. Resume and, at the lock screen, place the enrolled finger on the sensor
   immediately.
4. Observe the first scan is rejected; a second attempt a couple of seconds
   later succeeds.

## System details

- Omarchy version: 4.0.2-1
- Laptop: Lenovo ThinkBook 14 G9 IRL
- Fingerprint sensor: Goodix 27c6:550a (match-on-chip; requires the
  proprietary TOD driver — not affected by driver choice, same behavior with
  `libfprint-tod` + `libfprint-2-tod1-goodix-v2` from AUR and official
  `fprintd`)
- `omarchy debug --no-sudo --print` output attached separately

## Notes

- SDDM is set to autologin for this user, so the session never actually
  prompts for fingerprint at the SDDM greeter — the first fingerprint prompt
  a user hits is Omarchy's own Quickshell lock screen right after session
  start or after resume, which is where this reproduces.
- Journal excerpt and full debug log are attached to this issue.

issues.title: Shell leaks VRAM on failed EGL context creation, causing Super+Space/menu to silently stop working (NVIDIA, low VRAM)
issues.body:
## Description

The Omarchy shell (`quickshell`) leaks VRAM on every failed layer-shell surface creation, instead of releasing the partial allocation. On a system with limited VRAM, this creates a self-reinforcing failure loop: once GPU memory is tight enough that one surface creation fails, every subsequent attempt (e.g. repeatedly pressing Super+Space to open the menu) leaks more VRAM and makes recovery less likely, until `omarchy restart shell` is run to reclaim it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Omarchy on a machine with a small-VRAM discrete GPU shared across several GPU-memory-hungry apps (in my case: an NVIDIA GTX 1050 with 2GB VRAM, alongside Chromium, VS Code, and other Electron apps).
2. Let GPU memory usage climb until there isn't enough free VRAM for `quickshell` to allocate a new EGL/GL context (I hit this around 1729/2048 MiB used, ~85%).
3. Press `SUPER + SPACE` (Omarchy menu) — nothing appears.
4. Keep pressing it — the shell keeps trying, keeps failing, and its own VRAM footprint keeps growing with each failed attempt (in my case: 392 MiB right after a clean shell restart, growing to 702 MiB, then 811 MiB within ~2 minutes, without a single successful render).

## Expected behavior

- A failed layer-shell surface creation should not leak the partially-allocated GPU resources.
- Ideally, quickshell would detect repeated `EGL_BAD_ALLOC` / "Failed to create graphics context" failures and either back off, or the Omarchy supervisor would notice sustained failure and auto-restart the shell (similar to the recovery gap noted in #8491, though that issue is about a different trigger — EGL context loss on resume — this one is triggered purely by VRAM exhaustion, no suspend/resume involved).

## Actual behavior

`SUPER + SPACE` (and any other menu/panel toggle) silently does nothing. The keybinding and IPC call both succeed — `hyprctl binds` shows the bind is correctly registered, and `omarchy-menu toggle root` returns exit 0 — but no surface is ever rendered. journalctl shows repeated:

```
WARN: QWaylandGLContext::makeCurrent: eglError: 0x3003
WARN: QRhiGles2: Failed to make context current. Expect bad things to happen.
WARN: Failed to create RHI (backend 2)
ERROR: Failed to create graphics context for qs::wayland::layershell::WlrLayershell(...): "Failed to initialize graphics backend for OpenGL."
```

Only `omarchy restart shell` recovers it (until VRAM fills up again).

## System details

- Omarchy: 4.0.3-1
- Hyprland: 0.56.2
- Quickshell: 0.3.1
- Kernel: 7.2.3-arch1-3
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050, 2048 MiB VRAM, driver 580.178.04

## Notes

Possibly related to #8491 (shell stops rendering after resume-time `EGL_BAD_CONTEXT` on NVIDIA) — same failure class (Qt RHI/EGL context loss on NVIDIA with no automatic recovery), but a different trigger (VRAM exhaustion under normal use vs. suspend/resume).

issues.title: Shell config mutations rewrite shell.json from in-memory state — concurrent/external edits silently lost, service plugins[] entries vanish
issues.body:
### System details

Intel Core i7-1260P (Framework Laptop 13), Intel Iris Xe iGPU, Omarchy 4.0.3-1, Hyprland 0.56.2, quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7-3

### What's wrong?

`~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` is rewritten **whole-file from in-memory state** by every shell-side config mutation, so any concurrent or external edit the shell hasn't ingested is silently clobbered. In practice this deletes `plugins[]` entries — and a missing `plugins[]` entry for a service plugin means it silently never loads again.

Mechanism (quattro, `shell/shell.qml:162`):

```js
function mutateShellConfig(mutator) {
  var copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(shellConfig || builtinShellConfig))
  mutator(copy)
  persistShellConfig(copy)
}
```

- `shellConfig` is only as fresh as the last `applyShellConfig()`. The `userConfigFile` FileView watch → `reload()` path is asynchronous, so an external writer that touches shell.json shortly before a shell-side mutation can lose the race: the next `enablePlugin` / `setPluginEnabled` / bar-move / settings mutation persists the stale in-memory copy over it.
- External writers are normal in Omarchy flows: `omarchy plugin add/update/remove` (driven by the plugin-manager bar widget) run `omarchy-shell-config`-based jq rewrites; migrations and `omarchy refresh shell` rewrite the file; users edit it by hand. With multiple writers, this is last-writer-wins with no merge and no warning.

Observed incident (real data loss, today):

- A third-party service plugin (`kinds: ["service"]`, entry point `Service.qml`) had a `plugins[]` entry in shell.json. Proven present: the shell instance started at 13:03 loaded it and mapped its layer surface (`openlayer` event in the quickshell log).
- At 14:12 a plugin install/enable flow rewrote shell.json; afterwards `plugins[]` contained only the newly enabled plugin. The service plugin's entry was gone.
- On the next shell restart the service plugin silently never loaded — service plugins require a `plugins[]` entry, they have no bar widget, and nothing is logged. Restoring the entry + `omarchy restart shell` brought it back.

Steps to recreate:

1. `omarchy plugin enable <service-plugin>` (or add its id to `plugins[]`) and restart the shell.
2. While the shell is running, externally edit shell.json (e.g. `jq` adding a harmless key), then immediately trigger a shell-side mutation (a bar drag-reorder, `omarchy-shell shell enablePlugin ...`, or a plugin toggle from the plugin manager). If the mutation runs before the FileView reload lands, the persisted copy is the stale in-memory one and the external edit is gone.
3. Even without the race: any external edit inotify misses is silently lost on the next shell-side mutation.

Note: sequential shell-side mutations alone don't lose data (each `persistShellConfig` updates `shellConfig`); the hazard is any write the shell didn't ingest before the next mutation.

Suggested fixes (any of):

1. Make `mutateShellConfig` read-modify-write from the current on-disk file (re-parse `userConfigFile.text()` fresh, falling back to in-memory only if unreadable) instead of the cached `shellConfig`.
2. Before persisting, verify the on-disk text still matches the last-ingested content (cheap string compare); if it differs, re-ingest and re-apply the mutation, or fail loudly instead of persisting.
3. At minimum, log a warning whenever a persist is about to overwrite content that differs from the last-known ingest — the silence is the worst part.

Related: #8357 is the upgrade-time version of the same hazard (force-overwrite instead of migrate); this report is the runtime-mutation cousin.

issues.title: Hermes setup: Nous unavailable-model list hides selectable rows, making arrow navigation appear frozen
issues.body:
### System details

Omarchy 4.0.3-1; Hermes Agent package 0.19.0 (Omarchy mise wrapper, Python 3.13); Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2 (xterm-ghostty); kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3; Intel Core Ultra 9 285; Intel Arrow Lake-S graphics + NVIDIA RTX A1000

### What's wrong?

Launching Hermes through Omarchy's AI agent selector, starting setup, and choosing **Nous** reaches a ‘Select default model’ screen that appears frozen: Up/Down produces no visible selection change.

This is a verified layout defect in the installed Hermes dependency, reported here because it blocks the Hermes onboarding flow exposed by Omarchy. The fix likely belongs upstream in Hermes; no defect in Omarchy's keyboard forwarding was established.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Omarchy's AI agent selector and select Hermes.
2. Start setup and choose Nous.
3. Reach model selection with enough unavailable-model information to fill the terminal.
4. Press Up/Down: selectable choices and their cursor are off-screen.

The account tier was not independently inspected. The same failure was reproduced without credentials using a long description in the menu implementation.

### Expected

Navigation hints and selectable rows remain visible regardless of the length of the unavailable-model list.

### Confirmed cause

In `hermes_cli/auth.py`, `_prompt_model_selection()` puts unavailable models in the description passed to `curses_radiolist()`. In `hermes_cli/curses_ui.py`, `curses_radiolist()._draw_header()` allows that description to consume almost the entire terminal height, then returns a starting row for choices below the drawable area. Arrows still move the cursor internally, but the cursor and choices cannot be drawn.

### Minimal reproduction (no account/network required)

Run with Hermes's Python interpreter in a terminal approximately 24 rows tall:

```python
from hermes_cli.curses_ui import curses_radiolist

result = curses_radiolist(
    'Select default model:',
    ['Available model A', 'Available model B'],
    description='\n'.join(
        'Unavailable model ' + str(i) for i in range(30)
    ),
)
print('SELECTED', result)
```

Before the fix, only the description and navigation hint are visible. Down followed by Enter returns index 1, proving that keyboard input works while the selection is invisible.

### Tested local fix

Limit the description height and reserve space for the choices. Replace the description loop inside `curses_radiolist()._draw_header()` with:

```python
description_budget = max(0, max_y - 8)
visible_description = desc_lines[:description_budget]
if len(desc_lines) > description_budget and visible_description:
    omitted = len(desc_lines) - description_budget + 1
    visible_description[-1] = (
        f'  ... {omitted} more information lines hidden'
    )
for dline in visible_description:
    stdscr.addnstr(row, 0, dline, max_x - 1, curses.A_NORMAL)
    row += 1
```

After this change, the same 24-row reproduction displays both choices, Down visibly moves to the second choice, and Enter returns index 1. The patch was applied locally with a backup; after relaunching Hermes, the affected user confirmed that it fixed the actual Nous setup problem. A package update may overwrite this workaround.

### Diagnostics

`omarchy debug --no-sudo --print` was attempted, but this installation reports ‘Unknown Omarchy command’; no `omarchy-debug` binary was found under `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/`. The minimal reproduction isolates the problem without account logs.

Report prepared with Codex from local source inspection, terminal reproduction, and user confirmation.

issues.title: Third-party bar-widgets never receive barWidgetRegistry, so a widget cannot host other widgets
issues.body:
A third-party **bar-widget** never receives `barWidgetRegistry`, and the `PluginBarApi` facade it gets as `bar` doesn't expose one either. A widget that hosts other widgets — a tray with a drawer, a group, an overflow menu — therefore has no way to resolve the components it is meant to show.

I don't know whether this is a deliberate narrowing or an oversight, so this is a question as much as a report.

## What a bar-widget receives

`Bar.qml`'s `injectProps()` injects exactly three properties:

https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml#L1999-L2006

```js
function injectProps() {
  var target = activeItem
  if (!target) return
  if ("bar" in target) target.bar = firstParty
    ? root : root.pluginBarApiFor(pluginApiId, moduleName, registered)
  if ("moduleName" in target) target.moduleName = moduleName
  if ("settings" in target) target.settings = moduleSettings
}
```

For a third-party widget, `bar` is the `PluginBarApi` facade, whose surface is tooltips, click targets, popouts, panel switching, `_run`, `_setCenterHoverRevealSuppressed`, and `_moduleWidgets`:

https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml#L250-L270

`_moduleWidgets` looks close but isn't it — it returns the plugin's **own** live instances across monitors, and only for its own module name:

```js
_moduleWidgets: function(requestedId) {
  return String(requestedId || "") === String(moduleName || "")
    ? root.moduleWidgets(moduleName) : []
}
```

## Where the registry does get injected

`shell.qml` injects `barWidgetRegistry` at three sites — the bar itself, service instances, and panel loaders:

- `configureBar` — https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/shell.qml#L223
- service instantiation — https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/shell.qml#L920
- panel loader — https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/shell.qml#L1333

`pluginBarWidgetRegistryFor` already builds a detached, capability-scoped snapshot for third parties, so the safe object exists:

https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/quattro/shell/shell.qml#L755-L772

It just never reaches the bar-widget instantiation path — the one place that would need it to host anything.

## Effect

`io.github.tyrichards.tray` declares `property var barWidgetRegistry` and reads `root.barWidgetRegistry || (root.bar ? root.bar.barWidgetRegistry : null)`. Both are null, so its drawer resolves 0 of the 8 widgets it is configured to hold. Instrumented in a local fork:

```
[tray] entries=8 hosted=8 hasContent=true registry=NULL resolved=0
```

`agents/skills/shell-dev.md` says entry points accept `pluginRegistry` / `barWidgetRegistry` "as appropriate", which reads as though a bar-widget could ask for one.

## Question

Is widget-hosting meant to be a full-bar-only capability now? If so, the docs could say so, and a bar-widget asking for `barWidgetRegistry` could be warned rather than silently handed null — the failure is invisible until someone opens the drawer.

If it isn't deliberate, adding the same `if ("barWidgetRegistry" in target) target.barWidgetRegistry = ...` line to `injectProps` (through `pluginBarWidgetRegistryFor`, so third parties keep the detached snapshot) would restore it without widening what a widget can reach. Happy to send that PR.

---
Reported with the help of Claude Code.

issues.title: Bluetooth panel feeds live device lists to Repeaters, crashing the shell on a device-list change (mid-incubation use-after-free in Qt)
issues.body:
## What happened

quickshell (running the Omarchy shell) SIGSEGV'd at 13:09:14. The shell auto-restarted; no data is lost.

About 3 seconds earlier the user toggled the Bluetooth adapter off (`rfkill` block at 13:09:11; BlueZ `PowerState` -> `Blocked`, `Powered` -> `false`). The user then clicked in the shell. The stack proves the mechanism:

- mouse release -> signal handler -> QML binding update -> `QQuickRepeater::setModel` -> `regenerate()`
- Repeater mid-incubation: `QQmlIncubatorPrivate::incubate` -> `QQmlObjectCreator::createInstance` -> `Module::evaluate`
- fault in `QV4::Runtime::TypeofName::call` -> `QObjectWrapper::getQmlProperty` on an already-freed QObject -- **use-after-free in `libQt6QmlModels` / Qt 6.11.2**

`onConnectedDevicesChanged` / `onKnownDevicesChanged` / `onDiscoveredDevicesChanged` mutate the Repeater models (`connectedRows`, `scrollRows`) synchronously off a BlueZ signal, so a change can land mid-QML-incubation and the Repeater rebuilds against a freed object.

## Why this is Omarchy's to fix

The root fault is in the Qt QML engine, but Omarchy already ships mitigations for exactly this race in its own panels:

- `plugins/panels/audio/Panel.qml` (~line 103) -- snapshot timer; comment: "rebuilding a Repeater from that signal path has crashed"
- `plugins/notifications/Service.qml` (~line 188) -- `Qt.callLater`; comment: "avoids crashes when a Repeater is mid-incubation while we mutate its model"

The Bluetooth panel (`plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml`, Repeater ~line 783 and ListView ~line 817) is the one panel still feeding live models straight into a Repeater/ListView without that protection.

## Expected

Bluetooth adapter power toggle or device connect/disconnect should update the panel without crashing.

## Proposed fix

Apply the same snapshot-timer pattern the audio panel uses: feed `displayConnectedRows` / `displayScrollRows` snapshots, debounced ~75 ms, refreshed on open and on device-list change, cleared on close; cursor logic keeps reading the live lists so nothing points at a stale index. The modified file is validated (balanced, mirrors the audio panel) and staged on the reporter's machine.

## Known upstream reports

Same bug reported against the quickshell mirror repo:

- #965 -- crash on Bluetooth device disconnection
- #970 -- crash on a click while the Bluetooth device list is changing

This report adds that it still reproduces on quickshell 0.3.1 / Qt 6.11.2.

# Hard freeze shortly after resuming from s2idle on Intel Ice Lake (i915) with kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3

## Summary

On Omarchy 4.0.3-1 with kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3, this laptop intermittently
hard-freezes **~20-50 s after a successful s2idle resume**. Suspend and resume
both complete and log normally (`PM: suspend entry` and `PM: suspend exit`); the
machine then runs briefly (networking reconnects, the shell re-registers its QML
plugins) and stops logging entirely. No panic, oops, watchdog, MCE or lockup

(7.1.9-arch1-2) without freezing right after a resume**. The regression appeared
after the in-place update to 7.2.3-arch1-3 on 2026-09-08 23:10.

This is a *different* failure mode from the other 7.2.3 suspend reports: here the
machine resumes (`PM: suspend exit` is present) and dies shortly afterward, on
Intel Ice Lake, with `s2idle` (not `deep`).

## System details

- **Omarchy**: 4.0.3-1
- **Kernel**: 7.2.3-arch1-3 (updated in place from 7.1.9-arch1-2 on 2026-09-08 23:10)
- **linux-firmware**: 20260810-2
- **Machine**: ASUSTeK ZenBook UX325JA, firmware UX325JA.312 (2022-01-17)
- **CPU/GPU**: Intel Core i7-1065G7 (Ice Lake), Iris Plus Graphics G7 `[8086:8a52]`, driver `i915`
- **`/sys/power/mem_sleep`**: `[s2idle] deep` (s2idle default; the freeze happens under s2idle)
- **Desktop**: Hyprland 0.56.2, SDDM
- **Display**: external monitor on HDMI-A-1 active, eDP-1 off
- **journald**: persistent (`/var/log/journal` present), so a stopped log is a real halt, not a lost-log artifact

## What happens

1. Suspend (lid close / idle) completes normally: `PM: suspend entry (s2idle)`.
2. Resume completes normally: `PM: suspend exit`, and userspace comes back.
3. ~20-50 s later the whole machine hard-freezes: the journal simply stops.
4. Forced power-off; next boot shows no clean-shutdown record.

### Most recent occurrence (2026-09-12, boot `fb822a61`'s predecessor)

```text
Sep 12 07:30:43 omarchy kernel: PM: suspend entry (s2idle)
Sep 12 07:30:48 omarchy kernel: PM: suspend exit
... tailscaled reconnects, NetworkManager-dispatcher, timesyncd ...
Sep 12 07:31:17 omarchy kernel: [UFW BLOCK] ...      <-- last line of the boot
Sep 12 07:34:19 omarchy kernel: Linux version 7.2.3-arch1-3   <-- next boot
```

### Previous occurrence (2026-09-10)

```text
Sep 10 07:06:19 omarchy kernel: PM: suspend entry (s2idle)
Sep 10 07:06:23 omarchy kernel: PM: suspend exit
... voxtype gdk_monitor_set_scale assertions, omarchy-shell QML plugin warnings ...
Sep 10 07:07:13 omarchy kernel: <-- last line of the boot
Sep 10 07:08:32 omarchy kernel: Linux version 7.2.3-arch1-3   <-- next boot
```

## Suspends per kernel (retained journal)

| Boot | Kernel | `PM: suspend entry` | `PM: suspend exit` | Outcome |
|------|--------|--------------------:|-------------------:|---------|
| -5 | 7.1.9 | 24 | 24 | ran to a normal end |
| -4 | 7.1.9 | 11 | 11 | ran to a normal end |
| -3 | 7.1.9 | 7 | 7 | ran to a normal end |
| -2 | 7.2.3 | 2 | 2 | froze ~50 s after the last exit |
| -1 | 7.2.3 | 3 | 3 | froze ~29 s after the last exit |

So the freeze is **not** a missing `PM: suspend exit` — resume succeeds and the
machine dies shortly afterwards.

## Not the cause

- **Not OOM**: at the 2026-09-12 death `mem_available` was ~4.4 GiB; the local
  crash ledger recorded `suspected_oom=False` and `swap_used` ~2.7 GiB.
- **No `i915` "Unclaimed access detected prior to suspending"** warning anywhere in
  the journal (count 0), unlike #11255.
- **No kernel panic/oops, no MCE, no soft lockup/hung task** — the log simply stops.
- High-ish thermals (package ~67-78 °C, `crit` 100 °C) but not at critical, and the
  same temps occur on clean-booting sessions.

## Related issues

- #11255 — Intel Raptor Lake-P, `i915`, kernel 7.2.3, *deep* suspend never resumes
  (hard hang at *entry*; here it resumes first).
- #11332 — intermittent s2idle resume failure, more frequent on 7.2.3 (AMD HP
  EliteBook; hangs at *entry*).
- #11245 — kernel 7.2.3 regression (ELAN touchpad), A/B confirmed vs linux-lts.
- #7380 — omarchy-shell crashes and relaunches on wake (FALLBACK monitor removal).
  The same shell crash is visible here during the suspend/wake path, but it
  self-heals and is separate from the hard freeze.

## Possible workarounds to test

- Pin/downgrade to kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2 (or use `linux-lts`) until a fixed kernel
  is available.
- Try `i915.enable_psr=0` / `i915.enable_dc=0`, since the failure is in the
  post-resume display re-initialisation path.
- Try `mem_sleep_default=deep` to move off s2idle.

## Diagnostics

`omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print` captured (system info, package list, cmdline,
CPU/GPU) and saved locally at `/tmp/omarchy-debug.log`.
