issues.title: BCM43602 WiFi signal extremely weak (-90 dBm) on MacBook Pro 2015-2017
issues.body:
# BCM43602 WiFi signal extremely weak (-90 dBm) on MacBook Pro 2015-2017

## Hardware

- MacBookPro13,3 (2016, 15" Touch Bar) and similar 2015-2017 models
- Broadcom BCM43602 (PCI ID: 14e4:43ba, rev 02)
- Omarchy 4.x / kernel 7.2.x

## Problem

WiFi signal is extremely weak — **-90 dBm** at 1 meter from router. The card associates but the signal is unusable past ~1 meter.

```
$ iw dev wlp3s0 link
signal: -90 dBm
rx bitrate: 54.0 MBit/s
tx bitrate: 36.0 MBit/s
```

## Root Cause

The `brcmfmac` driver loads a generic NVRAM config that lacks proper power amplifier settings and antenna gain parameters for the MacBook's hinge-antenna design.

## What Didn't Fix It

1. `options brcmfmac feature_disable=0x82000` — fixes WPA handshake, NOT signal
2. `options cfg80211 ieee80211_regdom=US` — fixes regulatory domain, NOT signal
3. `roamoff=1` — reduces scanning retries, NOT signal
4. NVRAM config from Andy Holst (Bugzilla #193121) — helps channels, NOT signal

All help with **connecting** but NOT **signal strength**.

## Solution

Install [cristianmiranda's improved NVRAM config](https://gist.github.com/cristianmiranda/ba9d64b4324f0803d9422d765de62252) which has proper board flags, antenna gain, and power amplifier parameters specific to MacBookPro13,3:

```bash
curl -fLO https://gist.githubusercontent.com/cristianmiranda/ba9d64b4324f0803d9422d765de62252/raw/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt
sed -i "s/^macaddr=.*/macaddr=$(cat /sys/class/net/wlp3s0/address)/" brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt
sudo install -Dm644 brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt /usr/lib/firmware/brcm/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt
sudo limine-mkinitcpio
sudo reboot
```

## Result

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Signal | -90 dBm | -58 dBm |
| 5GHz speed | Unusable | 360 MBit/s |

32 dBm improvement — 5GHz now works reliably at full speed.

## PR

https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11620

/cc @adamavenir (existing Broadcom fix in #1022)
/cc @andyholst (Bugzilla #193121 NVRAM config)

issues.title: Tray: add a monochrome icon setting, with a documented app-side contract
issues.body:
Proposal, not a bug report, and deliberately not a PR: I could not make a widget-side reskin that was worth shipping (see below), so this is a design question first.

Follows on from #8845 (icons are only tinted when the name ends in `-symbolic`) and #8159 (colorization cannot lighten a dark fill). #8844 and #7288 are the neighbouring cases.

## What happens today

- `omarchy.tray` tints an icon only when its name ends in `-symbolic`.
- Chromium publishes its tray icon as a raw bitmap with no `IconName` at all, so **every Electron tray app is structurally excluded** from tinting (ChatGPT, Proton Pass, Slack, Discord, Spotify, ...). D-Bus dump in #8845.
- The widget's only colour maths is `MultiEffect.colorization` (`rgb = ink * luma(src)`, alpha untouched). It cannot lighten a dark source (#8159) and cannot preserve the detail inside a tile-shaped bitmap, so "tint everything" is not available either.
- `SystemTrayItem.id` is the SNI `Id`, and Chromium hardcodes `chrome_status_icon_1` for all of them, so a per-app setting cannot address them individually.

Result: on a monochrome bar, a couple of brand-coloured icons that nothing in the shell can do anything about.

## Proposal

1. **A tray setting** (name to your taste - `monochrome`, `trayMonochrome`, or a `tray.iconStyle` enum) that, when enabled, prefers a monochrome rendering of any tray item that offers one and draws it in the bar ink. Existing `-symbolic` tinting stays as it is.

2. **A documented app-side contract**, because the widget cannot manufacture a monochrome icon: an app opts in by publishing an `IconName` that resolves in the icon theme (with a `-symbolic` variant) rather than a bitmap alone. That is the half that belongs to app producers - realistically a request to Chromium, since its behaviour is what forces every Electron app to ship a pixmap.

3. **Leave icons untouched when no monochrome form exists** - do not synthesise one. Of the three options I measured, a coloured but recognisable icon is the least bad.

## Why not a patch from me

I built and measured all three renderings on a real bar (flat silhouette, ink x luma, and luminance-normalise-then-ink). The best lands on the bar ink with the detail preserved, but it is still the widget inventing artwork the app never supplied, and at 12px it reads worse than the app's own icon. I reverted it and left the stock widget in place rather than send a reskin - happy to test whatever direction you prefer instead.

## Questions

- Do you want the setting at all, or is the intended answer "icon theme / app side only, no widget change"?
- If yes: does the contract belong in the tray widget, in the icon theme convention, or in the plugin API so other bar widgets can honour it too?
- Any preference on naming (`monochrome` vs `iconStyle`)?

Happy to verify a patch on omarchy 4.0.3 / quickshell 0.3.1 / Qt 6.11.2 (Arch + Hyprland, transparent bar), with real tray items rather than a mock.

issues.title: omarchy-menu-images reuses stale thumbnails after an image is overwritten in place
issues.body:
### System details

Code-level reproduction on macOS with Bash; reviewed commit b679363bed05415771a1b1dc92c6899a908236f7. No installed Omarchy desktop or omarchy-debug output; scope and stat adapter described below.

### What's wrong?

## Summary

`omarchy-menu-images` reuses cached thumbnail rows after an existing image is overwritten in place. The fast signature only includes each directory's mtime, which does not change when the contents of an existing file change. A cache hit then bypasses the per-file size/mtime checks and keeps the old thumbnail path.

This is an AI-assisted code-review report. The cache-decision block was reproduced in isolation on macOS, not in a running Omarchy desktop. No claim of end-to-end GUI testing is intended.

## Affected code

Reviewed commit: `b679363bed05415771a1b1dc92c6899a908236f7`.

- [Directory-only signature and early cache hit](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/b679363bed05415771a1b1dc92c6899a908236f7/bin/omarchy-menu-images#L121-L143)
- [Per-image signature used when thumbnail_for actually runs](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/b679363bed05415771a1b1dc92c6899a908236f7/bin/omarchy-menu-images#L201-L214)

## Isolated reproduction

Run the following with Bash from a checkout of the reviewed commit. All fixtures are created in a new temporary directory. The cached row and media bytes are synthetic: this tests invalidation, not decoding or the UI. The macOS adapter only changes how the directory mtime is read; Linux uses GNU stat directly.

```bash
review_source="$PWD/bin/omarchy-menu-images"
review_root=$(mktemp -d)
review_images="$review_root/images"
mkdir "$review_images"
printf 'old image bytes' >"$review_images/example.png"

if [[ $(uname -s) == Darwin ]]; then
  stat() { command stat -f '%m' "$3"; }
fi

image_dirs=("$review_images")
rows_cache_file="$review_root/cached.rows"
rows_fast_signature_file="$review_root/cached.fast-signature"
review_mtime=$(stat -Lc '%Y' "$review_images")
printf '%s\t%s' "$review_images/example.png" old-thumbnail.jpg >"$rows_cache_file"
printf 'v3\n%s:%s\n' "$review_images" "$review_mtime" >"$rows_fast_signature_file"

printf 'new image bytes with a different size' >"$review_images/example.png"
[[ $(stat -Lc '%Y' "$review_images") == "$review_mtime" ]] || exit 1
rows_fast_signature=$'v3\n'
rows_signature=$'v4\n'
rows_cache_hit=false
image_files=()
rows=''

# Exact cache-decision block at the commit linked above.
eval "$(sed -n '121,143p' "$review_source")"
printf 'rows_cache_hit=%s\nrows=%s\n' "$rows_cache_hit" "$rows"
printf 'Test fixtures retained at %s\n' "$review_root"
```

Observed output (temporary paths shortened):

```text
rows_cache_hit=true
rows=/tmp/.../images/example.png<TAB>old-thumbnail.jpg
```

The changed file size is never examined because the directory-only signature still matches. The subsequent row-building code is gated by `rows_cache_hit != true`, so it cannot regenerate the thumbnail on this path.

## Expected behavior / user impact

After an existing wallpaper or preview image is saved in place, reopening the selector should invalidate the corresponding thumbnail. Currently the cache decision continues to select the previous thumbnail until another event invalidates the directory cache. Editors that save by atomic replacement may change the directory mtime and therefore not trigger this case.

## Related work

The "Note on staleness" in #8922 explicitly mentions this existing limitation. That PR addresses unreadable images and index performance, rather than invalidation of successfully cached images changed in place. Searches for existing image-selector/thumbnail issues did not find a dedicated report for this behavior; please link one if this is already tracked.

## Possible fix

Check cached media files' metadata before trusting the row cache, or use content-change notifications to invalidate it. A regression test should populate a successful row cache, overwrite an existing image with a different size without changing the directory mtime, and verify that the old thumbnail is no longer reused.

issues.title: screenrecording --with-webcam: overlay mpv is orphaned when the camera never delivers a frame; cleanup only sends SIGTERM and a second --stop-recording exits 1
issues.body:
## System details

Dell XPS (Panther Lake), Intel Core Ultra X7 358H, Intel Arc B390 (integrated), Omarchy 4.0.3-1 stable, kernel 7.2.3-arch1-1-ptl, `intel-ipu7-camera` 1.0.5-1. Webcam is the OV08X40 behind Intel IPU7, exposed to userspace as the v4l2loopback node `/dev/video50` fed by `v4l2-relayd@ipu7`.

## What's wrong?

When the webcam device opens but never delivers a frame, `omarchy capture screenrecording --with-webcam` leaves a frozen mpv `WebcamOverlay` window on screen that Omarchy cannot remove, and the user has no supported way to get rid of it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a camera device that opens but produces no frames. Any IPU6/IPU7 machine hit by #10837 does this today: `v4l2-relayd` opens the loopback, its `icamerasrc` pipeline fails, so readers of `/dev/video50` block forever. `timeout 5 v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video50 --stream-mmap --stream-count=3` hanging until the timeout is enough to confirm the precondition.
2. `Super + Space` → capture → screen recording with webcam (or `omarchy capture screenrecording with webcam`).
3. Record for a while, then stop with the same binding or `omarchy capture screenrecording --stop-recording`.

### Observed

- The recording itself is fine. The mp4 is saved with video and audio and the "Screen recording saved" toast appears.
- The overlay window (178x200, title `WebcamOverlay`, app-id `WebcamOverlay-medium`) stays on screen, black, pinned in its corner.
- Running `--stop-recording` again does nothing: `screenrecording_active` is false (gpu-screen-recorder already exited), so the script hits the `elif [[ $STOP_RECORDING == "true" ]]` branch and exits 1 without touching the overlay (`omarchy-capture-screenrecording` lines 284-285).
- The stuck mpv also holds `/dev/video50` open, so every other camera consumer gets `VIDIOC_REQBUFS returned -1 (Device or resource busy)` until it is killed.

Only `kill -9` removes it:

```
$ pgrep -af '^mpv'
1043170 mpv av://v4l2:/dev/video50 --profile=low-latency --untimed --no-cache --demuxer-lavf-o=video_size=1920x1080,framerate=30 --vf=lavfi=[crop=ih*8/9:ih] --title=WebcamOverlay --wayland-app-id=WebcamOverlay-medium --no-border --no-audio --no-osc --osd-level=0 --really-quiet
$ kill 1043170; sleep 1; pgrep -af '^mpv' | wc -l
1
$ kill -9 1043170; sleep 1; pgrep -af '^mpv' | wc -l
0
```

### Expected

Stopping the recording removes the overlay unconditionally, and an overlay whose camera never produces a frame gives up on its own with a notification instead of sitting there black.

### Cause

Two things in `bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording`:

1. `cleanup_webcam` (line 110-111) is only `pkill -f "WebcamOverlay"`, i.e. SIGTERM. mpv blocked inside the v4l2 demuxer open/read never gets back to its event loop to honour it. `stop_screenrecording` does call `cleanup_webcam`, so the intent is right; the signal is just not strong enough for this state.
2. `start_webcam_overlay` (line 86-93) launches mpv with no timeout on the first frame. It waits up to 2 s for the Hyprland client to *map*, which succeeds because mpv creates its window before it has any video, and then proceeds. Nothing later checks that frames ever arrived.

Side note for anyone reproducing: `pkill -f WebcamOverlay` from an interactive shell also matches the shell's own command line and kills it. `pkill -9 -f '^mpv.*WebcamOverlay'` is the safe form.

### Suggested fix

- In `cleanup_webcam`, escalate: `pkill -f '^mpv.*WebcamOverlay'`, wait briefly, then `pkill -9 -f '^mpv.*WebcamOverlay'` if it is still alive. That alone fixes the "can't quit it" half.
- Make the `--stop-recording` branch run `cleanup_webcam` even when no recorder is active, so a second press always clears leftovers.
- Optionally, in `start_webcam_overlay`, probe the device for a frame before launching mpv (e.g. `timeout 3 v4l2-ctl -d "$WEBCAM_DEVICE" --stream-mmap --stream-count=1`) and fall back to recording without the overlay plus a notification if it times out.

The underlying "camera delivers nothing" condition on this machine is the jsoncpp soname break tracked in #10837, plus a separate ov08x40 sensor-binding regression on kernel 7.2 that is filed against intel/ipu7-drivers. This report is only about the screenrecording script's handling of that state, which will recur with any dead camera device.

Reported with the help of Claude Code.

issues.title: Lunar Lake: intel-ipu7-camera is installed by detection but built for Panther Lake only — no camera on any Core Ultra 200V laptop, fix open since 09-09
issues.body:
### System details Dell Pro 14 Premium PA14250 — Intel Lunar Lake, Core Ultra 7 268V, Arc 140V (xe); IPU7 8086:645d; OV08X40 (OVTI08F4) + HM1092 IR; Intel CVS bridge INTC10DE = Synaptics SVP7500 06cb:0701; Omarchy 4.0.4-1, linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3, intel-ipu7-camera 1.0.6-2 ### What's wrong? ### Summary The built-in camera on Lunar Lake laptops has never worked on Omarchy, and the `intel-ipu7-camera 1.0.6-2` update (omarchy-pkgs#418, merged 2026-09-13) made it worse for the people who had fixed it themselves. The cause is a packaging decision, not a driver mystery: the package is installed on every IPU7 machine by hardware detection but built for Panther Lake only (`IPU_VERSIONS="ipu75xa"`), so the HAL plugin a Lunar Lake IPU needs (`ipu7x`) does not exist on the system. A fix has been open since 2026-09-09 — omarchy-pkgs#367, rebased today on top of 1.0.6-2 and verified — with the analysis in omarchy-pkgs#366. Neither has had a reply in a week, while the same PKGBUILD was reworked and released for Panther Lake. ### Why this is not one laptop Lunar Lake (Core Ultra 200V) is the generation right before Panther Lake and sits in exactly the thin, long-battery machines Omarchy is aimed at: Dell Pro 13/14 Premium, XPS 13 9350 and many others. Every one of them gets this package by detection, and the plugin their IPU asks for is not built, so the camera cannot work on any of them. The community fix pack's tracker alone has several people on the Dell Pro 13/14 Premium with this exact stack. Panther Lake got its 7.2 regression fixed in four days (#10948 → omarchy-pkgs#418). Lunar Lake has had no camera for as long as the package has existed. ### What's wrong, precisely Out of the box on 1.0.6-2, `journalctl -u v4l2-relayd@ipu7`: ``` CamHAL[ERR] HalAdaptor: load_camera_hal_library, failed to open library: /usr/lib/libcamhal/plugins/ipu7x.so: No such file or directory CamHAL[WAR] CameraParserInvoker: parseSensors: No sensors available ``` `libcamhal` selects its plugin by IPU generation. The proprietary half for `ipu7x` (`libia_aic-ipu7x.so` and the rest) is already shipped from `ipu7-camera-bins`; only the plugin the HAL loads is missing, and it builds from the same pinned commit with one more entry in `IPU_VERSIONS`. Second, the relay pipeline hardcodes `videoflip method=rotate-180` for a sensor that on this board is mounted upright (`camera_sensor_rotation = 0`, `camera_orientation = Front`), so once the plugin exists the picture is upside down in every app. Steps to reproduce: install Omarchy 4.0.4 on a Dell Pro 14 Premium, open anything that uses the camera. Nothing to configure, nothing to click. ### What the 1.0.6-2 update did on this machine Since 2026-09-09 this laptop had RGB, IR and the privacy LED working: the community pack ([jibsta210/svp7500-camera-fix-pack](https://github.com/jibsta210/svp7500-camera-fix-pack)) for the kernel side, the `ipu7x` plugin from omarchy-pkgs#367 for the HAL. 1.0.6-2 introduced its own `intel-cvs` DKMS module under the same module name; DKMS installed it over the pack's during `omarchy update`, `intel_cvs` deferred with `CSI init failed`, the sensor never got its I2C adapter, and RGB was dead on both installed kernels, so booting the previous kernel did not help. Nothing in the update said a same-named kernel module was being introduced; the loaded module's srcversion was the only clue, and finding it cost an evening. ### What works — verified today on 1.0.6-2 + linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3 The kernel half of #418 is right for Lunar Lake too: with the package's own `intel-cvs/1.0.6` and the in-tree `ipu-bridge`, `ov08x40` joins the media graph behind `Intel CVS` on this board exactly as on the XPS 14. With omarchy-pkgs#367 on top (build `ipu7x`, its CVS pad formats, no rotation on `INTC10DE`): sensor resolved by the HAL, 30 fps on `/dev/video50`, upright image in a browser, `makepkg` builds. Four more small things complete the camera on this board, each with evidence in omarchy-pkgs#366 and carried locally: a probe-order fix in `camera-init` (the sensor's I2C bus is still owned by the bridge firmware when its `sleep 2` expires), a one-flag quirk change in the in-tree `cvs` driver for the privacy LED, one upstream hunk in `ipu-bridge` for the HM1092 IR sensor (mainline 7.3), and the psys s2idle patch. I can send each as its own PR. ### Ask A decision on omarchy-pkgs#366 / #367: take the Lunar Lake half of the package, or say the platform is out of scope and stop installing the package on `INTC10DE` boards. Either is fine. Silence is the only outcome that helps nobody.

issues.title: omarchy-audio-tuning fronted-sink ignores community omarchy_speaker_tuning sinks
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`omarchy-audio-output-switch` skips the physical sink returned by `omarchy-audio-tuning fronted-sink` so a speaker-tuning filter is not listed as a second Speakers device. `fronted-sink` only returns a sink when `tuning_match` hits a **shipped DMI/SKU laptop** tuning.

Community plugins (e.g. [thefreshoffice/omarchy-speaker-calibrator](https://github.com/thefreshoffice/omarchy-speaker-calibrator)) already create `omarchy_speaker_tuning` with `playback.props.target.object` pointing at the real speakers. On a desktop `fronted-sink` prints nothing, so Ctrl+^ and the sound menu show Speakers + Headphones + the virtual sink (Pulse description empty → OSD \"null\"; Quickshell shows the graph title \"Calibrated Speakers — Protected\"). Selecting the hardware Speakers bypasses the EQ. Games that call Pulse `SetDefaultEndpoint` can do the same.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a plugin that provides `omarchy_speaker_tuning` (not an Omarchy SKU tuning).
2. Run `omarchy audio tuning fronted-sink` — empty.
3. Run `omarchy-audio-output-switch` — rotation includes both the virtual sink and the physical speakers.

## Expected Behavior

If `omarchy_speaker_tuning` is present, `fronted-sink` should return the sink that filter plays into (`omarchy-audio-output-sink omarchy_speaker_tuning` / `target.object`), even when no shipped laptop tuning matched.

Then stock Ctrl+^ and the stock audio panel hide the raw speakers for every community calibrator. Volume keys already resolve through the DSP sink via `omarchy-audio-output-sink`.

## Actual Behavior

`fronted-sink` requires `tuned_hardware_sink` → `tuning_match` → DMI/SKU. No match → empty → three outputs.

## Environment

- Omarchy 4.0.4
- Desktop USB speakers + USB-C headphones
- Plugin virtual sink `omarchy_speaker_tuning` active

Related plugin report: will link after this issue exists.

issues.title: Screensaver self-exits within ~1s, canceling the pending idle lock too
issues.body:
## What happened

The idle screensaver (`omarchy-launch-screensaver` / `omarchy-screensaver`) intermittently opens and then closes itself again about 1 second later, before it's ever perceptible on screen. Because the shell's idle service (`Service.qml`) treats the screensaver window closing as "the user dismissed it," it also cancels the *entire* pending idle cycle — including the separately-timed idle lock. So on affected cycles, neither the screensaver nor the idle lock actually happens.

Confirmed via `journalctl --user` (idle service debug logging), 3 real idle cycles logged in one session, `idle.screensaver=150`, `idle.lock=300`:

```
# Cycle 1 (worked correctly — screensaver stayed up ~2m10s until real dismissal)
idle-monitor: idle
idle-cycle-start: screensaver=150 lock=300
process-start: screensaver [...] || omarchy-launch-screensaver
idle-monitor: active
idle-monitor-active: screensaver cycle remains armed
process-exit: screensaver exitCode=0 status=0
... (~2m10s later, real user input) ...
idle-cycle-cancel: screensaver-dismissed
process-start: wake omarchy-system-wake

# Cycle 2 (bug — self-exits ~1.1s after launch, no real input)
idle-monitor: idle
idle-cycle-start: screensaver=150 lock=300
process-start: screensaver [...]
idle-monitor: active
idle-monitor-active: screensaver cycle remains armed
process-exit: screensaver exitCode=0 status=0
idle-cycle-cancel: screensaver-dismissed      # only ~1.1s after process-exit
process-start: wake omarchy-system-wake

# Cycle 3 (same bug, same ~1.1-1.2s timing)
```

## Root cause (traced)

`omarchy-screensaver`'s inner watchdog loop:

```bash
while pgrep -t "${tty#/dev/}" -x ttfx >/dev/null; do
  if read -n1 -t 1 || ! screensaver_in_focus; then
    exit_screensaver
  fi
done
```

`screensaver_in_focus()` checks `hyprctl activewindow -j | jq -e '.class == "org.omarchy.screensaver"'` once per second. On a race (window mapped but Hyprland hasn't settled focus onto it yet, or `follow_mouse=1` focus-follow timing), this check fails on its first poll and the script self-terminates via `exit_screensaver`, closing the window almost immediately after it opened.

The shell's idle service (`omarchy-shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml`, `handleScreensaverWindowClosed`) then correctly-by-design treats any screensaver window close during an active idle cycle as user dismissal and calls `cancelIdleCycle("screensaver-dismissed")`, which also stops the still-pending `lockTimer`. So the bug doesn't just hide the screensaver — it silently defeats idle-lock too.

## Expected

The screensaver should reliably stay up until real user input (keyboard/mouse) is received, and a spurious self-exit from the screensaver script should not be indistinguishable from a genuine user dismissal for lock-cancellation purposes.

## Environment

- Omarchy version: 4.0.4-1
- Kernel: 7.2.5-3-omarchy
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 Microsoft Surface (R) Edition
- GPU: AMD Picasso/Raven 2 (Radeon Vega, integrated)
- Machine: Microsoft Surface Laptop 3 (AMD 15" edition)
- Single monitor (eDP-1), `follow_mouse = 1` (Hyprland default)
- `ttfx` 0.3.2

## Workaround in use

Disabled the screensaver locally via `omarchy toggle screensaver off`, which removes the racy window-close path entirely and lets the idle lock fire reliably again.

issues.title: Hybrid AMD iGPU + NVIDIA dGPU with the external display on the dGPU: nvidia.lua exports NVIDIA VA-API while Aquamarine renders on the iGPU, and Omarchy never sets AQ_DRM_DEVICES (counter-case to #11173)
issues.body:
### System details

- **Omarchy:** 4.0.4-1 · **Hyprland:** 0.56.2 (`efb50993…`, `aq_0.15`) · **Aquamarine:** 0.15.0-2 · **uwsm:** 0.26.7-1
- **Kernel:** linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3 · **Driver:** `nvidia-open-dkms` 610.57.04-1
- **GPUs:**
  - `0000:01:00.0` NVIDIA TU117M GeForce GTX 1650 Mobile / Max-Q `[10de:1f9d]` → `nvidia`
  - `0000:06:00.0` AMD Renoir Radeon Vega iGPU `[1002:1636]` → `amdgpu`
- **Outputs:**
  - `DP-1` — Acer XV272U V3, 2560x1440@179.877 — on the **NVIDIA** card
  - `eDP-1` — Chimei Innolux internal panel, 1920x1080@144 — on the **AMD** iGPU

```
/sys/class/drm/card1 -> nvidia [0000:01:00.0]   card1-DP-1:      connected
/sys/class/drm/card2 -> amdgpu [0000:06:00.0]   card2-eDP-1:     connected
                                                card2-HDMI-A-1:  disconnected
```

All three detectors return true on this machine:

```
$ omarchy-hw-nvidia && echo yes        # yes
$ omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp && echo yes    # yes
$ omarchy-hw-hybrid-gpu && echo yes    # yes
```

### What's wrong?

This is the mirror image of #11173 / #11168 / #8215, and it constrains the fix being proposed there.

`default/hypr/nvidia.lua` exports the NVIDIA VA-API/GL stack whenever `omarchy-hw-nvidia` and `omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp` succeed:

```
LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia
NVD_BACKEND=direct
__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia
```

(confirmed present in client environments on this machine).

But **Omarchy never sets `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`** — `grep -rn 'AQ_DRM_DEVICES' /usr/share/omarchy/` returns nothing. So the render device is whatever Aquamarine picks by default, which here is the AMD iGPU, while the only external display is physically wired to the NVIDIA dGPU.

The result is a split pipeline: **compositing on AMD, video decode on NVIDIA (NVDEC), scanout back on NVIDIA.** Frames cross the PCIe bridge in both directions every frame. Chromium flickers on pages containing video; disabling hardware acceleration in the browser avoids it, which matches the cross-GPU dmabuf import failure in #11168.

The important difference from #11173: there, every display hangs off the iGPU, so "stop forcing NVIDIA VA-API" is the right answer. **Here it is the wrong answer** — NVIDIA genuinely owns the connected external output, so the correct resolution is to move the *render device* onto NVIDIA and keep NVIDIA VA-API. A fix that keys only on "is the iGPU rendering?" and drops `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME` would regress this machine. What both cases actually need is the same invariant: **the VA-API driver and the Aquamarine render device must agree, and the render device should be the GPU that owns the connected outputs.**

### There is no Omarchy-managed place to put `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`

Two constraints make this awkward for users to fix themselves:

1. `hl.env()` in `hypr/*.lua` is too late. Aquamarine reads `AQ_DRM_DEVICES` when it opens the DRM devices at compositor startup, before the Lua config env is applied.
2. `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` is overwritten by `omarchy-refresh-hyprland`, so even a comment parked there does not survive.

`~/.config/uwsm/env` works (uwsm's environment preloader runs before Hyprland), but nothing in Omarchy documents or manages it for this purpose.

### Two Aquamarine findings that I could not find reported anywhere

Once NVIDIA is made the primary renderer on this hardware, two further things bite. Neither appears in any existing issue I could find.

**1. The internal panel needs `AQ_MGPU_NO_EXPLICIT=1`.** `eDP-1` hangs off the AMD card, so with NVIDIA primary it can only light up through a cross-GPU (mgpu) buffer copy. Explicit sync on imported buffers is NVIDIA's weak spot, and the atomic commit fails:

```
atomic drm request: failed to commit: Invalid argument
```

`AQ_MGPU_NO_EXPLICIT=1` disables explicit sync on mgpu buffers only and brings the panel up. (`render:explicit_sync` was removed in Hyprland 0.50, so there is no config-level escape hatch — cf. #10350.)

**2. `AQ_NO_MODIFIERS=1` is a trap — it makes the screen go black.** It is the obvious next thing to try, and it applies to *every* GPU rather than just the mgpu path. NVIDIA's KMS then refuses modifier-less scanout buffers:

```
GBM: Allocated a new buffer ... XR24 with modifier 0xffffffffffffff : INVALID
drm: Failed to submit a buffer with drmModeAddFB2
drm: Buffer failed to import to KMS
```

Every mode on `DP-1` fails to commit, the output drops to `0x0`, and the screen stays black while Hyprland itself runs fine. Worth a warning next to any mgpu guidance.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Hybrid AMD iGPU + NVIDIA (GSP) dGPU laptop, with the **external** display wired to the dGPU and the internal panel on the iGPU.
2. Log in to a stock Omarchy session. `nvidia.lua` exports `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`; Aquamarine picks the AMD iGPU as render device.
3. Play a video in Chromium/Brave on the external monitor with hardware acceleration on → flicker.

### Workaround in use (verified, stable)

In `~/.config/uwsm/env`:

```bash
# Resolve by-path -> /dev/dri/cardN. by-path names must NEVER go into
# AQ_DRM_DEVICES directly: the variable is colon-separated and
# "pci-0000:01:00.0-card" contains colons (see #8776).
_aq_nvidia=$(readlink -f /dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000:01:00.0-card 2>/dev/null)
_aq_amd=$(readlink -f /dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000:06:00.0-card 2>/dev/null)
if [ -c "$_aq_nvidia" ] && [ -c "$_aq_amd" ]; then
  export AQ_DRM_DEVICES="$_aq_nvidia:$_aq_amd"
elif [ -c "$_aq_amd" ]; then
  export AQ_DRM_DEVICES="$_aq_amd"   # NVIDIA missing: don't lose the session
fi
unset _aq_nvidia _aq_amd

export AQ_MGPU_NO_EXPLICIT=1
```

Resulting session: `AQ_DRM_DEVICES=/dev/dri/card1:/dev/dri/card2`, both outputs up at native refresh, no Chromium flicker.

### Suggestions

- Make `nvidia.lua`'s VA-API/GL exports and the Aquamarine render device one decision instead of two independent ones, keyed on **which GPU drives the connected outputs** — this covers both this issue and #11173 without regressing either.
- Give `AQ_DRM_DEVICES` a supported, refresh-proof home (e.g. an Omarchy-managed `~/.config/uwsm/env` fragment), since `hypr/*.lua` structurally cannot host it.
- If NVIDIA-first ordering is ever auto-applied, pair it with `AQ_MGPU_NO_EXPLICIT=1` for iGPU-attached internal panels, resolve by-path names to `/dev/dri/cardN` (#8776), and document that `AQ_NO_MODIFIERS=1` black-screens NVIDIA scanout.

Related: #11173, #11168, #8215 (VA-API vs render device), #10350 (NVIDIA-first ordering), #8776 (colon parsing).

issues.title: usbcore autosuspend config has no effect (usbcore is built into the kernel)
issues.body:
## What happened

`/etc/modprobe.d/omarchy-usb-autosuspend.conf` (shipped by `omarchy-settings`) contains:

```
options usbcore autosuspend=-1
```

This has no effect. `usbcore` is built into the kernel (`CONFIG_USB=y`) in the
stock Arch `linux` package, and `/etc/modprobe.d/` is only consulted when a
module is *loaded*. Built-in code never goes through modprobe, so the option is
silently ignored.

## What was expected

USB autosuspend disabled system-wide, as the config file intends.

## Steps to reproduce

On any Omarchy install running the stock Arch kernel:

```bash
$ modinfo usbcore | head -2
name:           usbcore
filename:       (builtin)          # <- not a module

$ cat /sys/module/usbcore/parameters/autosuspend
2                                  # <- expected -1

$ grep usbcore /proc/cmdline
                                   # <- nothing; no kernel parameter set either
```

## Impact

USB devices still autosuspend. This is not cosmetic — it breaks USB Bluetooth
adapters: the adapter suspends while idle and tears down the active A2DP link,
producing a repeating connect/disconnect cycle every few minutes during audio
playback.

Observed on a Realtek RTL8822CU (`1358:c123`), where the adapter had accumulated
28 minutes of `runtime_suspended_time` since boot:

```bash
$ cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/3-2/power/runtime_suspended_time
1690842                            # ms

$ cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/3-2/power/autosuspend_delay_ms
2000
```

PipeWire also logged `spa.bluez5.sink.media: Missing completion reports for
packet: Bluetooth adapter firmware bug?` — HCI completion packets lost when the
adapter wakes mid-stream. Both symptoms stopped once autosuspend was actually
disabled.

## Suggested fix

A udev rule expresses the same intent and works regardless of whether `usbcore`
is built in:

```
# /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/50-omarchy-usb-autosuspend.rules
ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="usb", TEST=="power/control", ATTR{power/control}="on"
```

It also applies without a reboot, unlike the kernel-parameter alternative
(`usbcore.autosuspend=-1` on the kernel cmdline), which would otherwise be the
only way to make the current approach work.

## System details

- Omarchy 4.0.4-1 (`omarchy-settings` 4.0.4-1)
- Kernel: stock Arch `linux` 7.2.3.arch1-3

issues.title: omacalc's default window rule has no center/size, so it stays full-screen after floating back from SUPER+F fullscreen toggle
issues.body:
**What happened**

The default window rule for `omacalc` in `default/hypr/apps/system.lua` is:

```lua
o.window("omacalc", { float = true })
```

This only floats the window — it never sets `center` or a `size`. Sibling
app rules in the same file pair `float = true` with `center = true`
(Tensaku, LocalSend, Battle.net's launcher), and Steam's rule additionally
sets an explicit `size`. `omacalc` is the only entry in that group missing
both.

Because there's no size/center rule, once the window gets floated back
from a tiled/fullscreen state (e.g. via the default `SUPER+F` fullscreen
toggle, or `SUPER+T` after it was tiled), it keeps whatever geometry it
last had — including full-monitor size/position — instead of returning to
a small centered window. `hyprctl clients` reports `floating: 1` even
though the window visually still looks fullscreen, edge-to-edge, with no
gaps.

**What was expected**

`omacalc` should reopen (or return from fullscreen/tiling) as a small,
centered floating window, consistent with how Tensaku/LocalSend/Steam
behave.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open Omacalc (it opens floating but sized/positioned like a tiled
   window rather than centered).
2. Press `SUPER + F` (fullscreen toggle) to go fullscreen.
3. Press `SUPER + F` again to exit fullscreen.
4. The window returns to `floating: 1` but stays sized to the monitor /
   last tiled geometry instead of a small centered window.

**Workaround verified**

Adding this user override fixes it:

```lua
o.window("omacalc", { center = true, size = { 420, 640 } })
```

Suggests the real fix is adding `center = true` (and ideally an explicit
`size`) to the default `omacalc` rule in `system.lua`, matching the other
apps in that file.

**System details**

- Omarchy version: 4.0.4-1
- Hyprland: 0.56.2 (v0.56.2, commit efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f)

command on this installed version (4.0.4-1) — `omarchy commands --all`
doesn't list a `debug` group, so no diagnostic log/URL is attached.

issues.title: [Bug]: Low contrast / invisible comments and terminal muted colors under dark themes (Foot regular0=bg and muted contrast)
issues.body:
### System details
AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT, NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, Omarchy 4.0.0.r2158.gd174d4a-1, Linux 7.2.5-4-omarchy, Foot, Neovim (LazyVim)

### What's wrong?

#### Summary
Under certain dark themes (such as `japan-night` or custom themes derived from `colors.toml`), comments, line numbers, and dimmed text in Neovim and the Foot terminal are virtually invisible against the background. The text only becomes readable when the cursor line (`CursorLine`) passes over it, giving the appearance that text is invisible unless highlighted.

This stems from two interacting factors in the templating and theming pipeline:

1. **Foot template hardcodes `regular0 = background`**:
   In `/usr/share/omarchy/default/themed/foot.ini.tpl`:
   ```ini
   regular0={{ background_strip }}
   bright0={{ muted_strip }}
   ```
   - Setting ANSI black (`regular0`) to `background_strip` makes any CLI tool outputting color 0 completely invisible.
   - `bright0` is mapped to `muted_strip`. When themes define `muted` with very low luminance (for example, `muted = "#294857"` on `background = "#0b1b2b"` in `japan-night`), the contrast ratio is ~1.5:1, failing basic accessibility. Any terminal application printing gray/dimmed text becomes unreadable.

2. **Neovim `aether.nvim` + `transparency.lua` comment contrast**:
   - In `/usr/share/omarchy/default/themed/neovim.lua.tpl`, `muted` is passed to `aether.nvim`.
   - `aether.nvim` defines `Comment = { fg = c.muted }`.
   - Omarchy's `~/.config/nvim/plugin/after/transparency.lua` strips `Normal` background (`hl.bg = nil`). Because there is no background behind normal text, the low-contrast `muted` color renders directly against the dark terminal/wallpaper.
   - The only reason lines become visible when navigated is because `CursorLine` defines an opaque background (`guibg`), which suddenly provides enough contrast to read the text.

3. **Markdown conceal interaction**:
   In LazyVim, `conceallevel=3` (via `render-markdown.nvim`) hides HTML comments and syntax markers when the cursor is on other lines and reveals them only on the active line (anti-conceal). When paired with low comment contrast, users cannot distinguish whether text is invisible due to palette contrast or concealed by Neovim, and changing themes does not fix the hidden characters because `conceallevel` is an editor buffer state rather than a theme property.

---

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Apply a theme where `muted` is very close in luminance to `background` (e.g. `japan-night` where `background = "#0b1b2b"` and `muted = "#294857"`).
2. Open Foot terminal and run:
   ```bash
   printf "\e[30mThis is regular0\e[0m and \e[90mThis is bright0\e[0m\n"
   ```
   Notice that `regular0` is completely invisible, and `bright0` is almost unreadable.
3. Open a code file with comments or a markdown file with `<!-- comments -->` in Neovim (`nvim file.md`).
4. Notice that comments outside the current line are unreadable or invisible, but become legible the moment the cursor moves onto the line (via `CursorLine`).
5. Changing colorschemes (`:colorscheme`) does not reveal markdown comments because `conceallevel=3` keeps them concealed.

---

### How to Resolve
1. **Fix `foot.ini.tpl`**:
   Avoid mapping `regular0` directly to `background`. Provide a distinct color offset or separate `color0` from the terminal canvas background.
2. **Palette contrast baseline**:
   Ensure `colors.toml` definitions or the template compiler enforce a minimum WCAG contrast ratio (e.g., at least 4.5:1 or 3:1) for `muted` against `background`. In our local fix, bumping `muted` from `#294857` to `#68889e` immediately restored readability across Neovim and Foot while preserving the theme's aesthetic.
3. **Neovim Comment highlight fallback**:
   In `neovim.lua.tpl` or `aether.nvim`, ensure `Comment` has a readable fallback that accounts for transparent backgrounds (`make_transparent`).

issues.title: Screenshot picker's unbind takes the user's own binds on TAB/CTRL+TAB/RETURN/arrows with it
issues.body:
## What happened

`default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua` binds `RETURN`, `CTRL + RETURN`, `TAB`, `CTRL + TAB` and the four arrow keys while a `selection` layer is on screen, then removes them on `layer.closed` through the handles it kept:

```lua
-- Unbinding by key would take a same-key binding out of the user's own config
-- with it, so each handle is kept and removed individually.
...
for _, keybind in ipairs(selection_binds) do
  keybind:unbind()
end
```

The handle does not give that protection. `keybind:unbind()` removes **every** bind registered for that key and modifier set, not just the one the handle refers to — so a user binding on any of those keys is destroyed the first time the screenshot window picker opens and closes, and stays gone until the next `hyprctl reload`.

Here it took `CTRL + TAB`, which `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua` uses for a window switcher plugin. The switcher silently stopped responding; nothing in the Hyprland log, `hyprctl binds` simply had no `CTRL + TAB` entry any more. Taking one screenshot with the window picker is enough to do it, so the binding disappears during ordinary use and comes back after any config reload, which makes it look intermittent.

## Expected

The picker's temporary binds should be removed without touching identically-keyed binds from the user's own config.

## Steps to reproduce

Bind one of the borrowed keys in `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua`:

```lua
o.bind("CTRL + TAB", "Probe", "true")
```

Then, with no screenshot needed — any layer named `selection` triggers it:

```bash
hyprctl reload
hyprctl binds -j | grep -c '"description": "Probe"'   # 1
slurp & sleep 1; pkill slurp; sleep 1
hyprctl binds -j | grep -c '"description": "Probe"'   # 0
```

`PRINT` → window picker → capture does the same thing.

## Where the fault is

The `unbind()` behaviour is Hyprland's, not Omarchy's — it matches by key, and the handle is not a per-bind reference. Two binds on one chord, removing only the first handle, takes both:

```bash
hyprctl dispatch 'function()
  _G.a = hl.bind("CTRL + F13", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("true"), { description = "probe A" })
  _G.b = hl.bind("CTRL + F13", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("true"), { description = "probe B" })
end'
hyprctl binds -j | grep -c '"description": "probe'    # 2
hyprctl dispatch 'function() _G.a:unbind() end'
hyprctl binds -j | grep -c '"description": "probe'    # 0
```

So the comment in `utilities.lua` describes a guarantee the API does not currently provide. Whether that is fixed in Hyprland or worked around in Omarchy, the user-visible breakage is Omarchy's to notice: it ships the binds that borrow those chords.

A workaround that holds in user config, if it is useful to anyone hitting this before a fix lands: count the `selection` layers and rebind on a one-shot timer after the last one closes (the timer matters — Omarchy unbinds from its own handler for the same `layer.closed` event, and the order the two handlers run in is not ours to pick).

```lua
hl.on("layer.closed", function(layer)
  if layer.namespace ~= "selection" or selection_layers == 0 then return end
  selection_layers = selection_layers - 1
  if selection_layers > 0 then return end
  hl.timer(bind_window_switcher, { timeout = 50, type = "oneshot" })
end)
```

## Related

#7090 reports a different defect in the same block: the binds are registered for *any* layer-shell client that names its layer `selection`, not just `omarchy-capture-region`'s picker. Scoping the picker's binds properly would likely fix both.

## System

- Omarchy 4.0.4-1
- Hyprland 0.56.2-2 (v0.56.2, commit efb5099)

Filed by Claude Opus 5 via Claude Code.

issues.title: Clipboard-owner timeout can stall omarchy-shell overlays
issues.body:
## What happened

During a running desktop session, every Omarchy Shell overlay I opened, including the launcher and bar-plugin popups, visibly stalled for about one second before rendering.

The omarchy-shell journal contained repeated Qt Wayland clipboard-read timeouts during the affected interval:

```text
QWaylandDataOffer: timeout reading from pipe
QWaylandDataOffer: error reading data for mimeType text/plain;charset=utf-8
QWaylandDataOffer: error reading data for mimeType text/plain
```

The session had no CPU, memory, or I/O pressure bottleneck. After the clipboard selection was replaced with ordinary plain text from another application, the Shell immediately returned to normal responsiveness.

At the time of the incident, the clipboard also advertised normal text formats plus these application-specific formats:

```text
WeChat_RichEdit_Format
QQ_Unicode_RichEdit_Format
x-application-mimetype-xwechat
```

This is not intended as a WeChat-specific report: WeChat is only one observed selection owner. Any application that advertises a text format but stalls while serving it should not be able to make unrelated shell UI wait.

## Expected behavior

Clipboard-history capture should fail closed for an unresponsive selection owner: discard that history item after a short bounded timeout while leaving the launcher, bar popups, notifications, and other omarchy-shell UI responsive.

The original clipboard selection should not be overwritten or coerced to plain text. Rich-text consumers should retain their normal clipboard behavior.

## Observed recovery

Replacing the selection with ordinary plain text restored normal behavior immediately. A subsequent metadata-only `wl-paste --list-types` query completed in 3 ms and an `omarchy-shell shell ping` completed in 26 ms.

## Suggested direction

Please consider making clipboard acquisition independent from the Shell UI path and bounded for every selection owner, rather than maintaining an application-specific MIME blacklist:

1. Read only the requested plain-text representation for history.
2. Enforce a short timeout and size bound in a worker/process that cannot block Quickshell UI.
3. On timeout, malformed data, or worker failure, skip only that history entry.

A small standalone reproducer using a deliberately non-responsive Wayland data offer would be preferable to relying on a proprietary application. I do not yet have such a minimal reproducer, so this report documents the observed behavior and exact log evidence rather than claiming every rich-text application reproduces it.

## Environment

- Omarchy 4.0.4-1
- Hyprland 0.56.2-2
- Quickshell 0.3.1-1
- wl-clipboard 1:2.3.0-1
- Linux WeChat package 4.1.1.8-1 was the observed selection owner

5. Switch view to workspace 4. It is reported as occupied (window count > 0
   in the workspace indicator), but nothing is rendered there. The window
   group is gone from every workspace.
6. While on workspace 4 (visually empty), press Super+G (toggleGroup).
7. Hyprland crashes with SIGSEGV.

## Expected behavior

Either the group should remain intact/visible after an unrelated window is
moved onto its workspace, or, failing that, toggleGroup should not crash
when invoked in a workspace whose tracked window/group state is already
inconsistent.

## Actual behavior

Hyprland segfaults. Backtrace shows the crash inside
`Layout::CWindowTarget::assignToSpace()`, called from
`Desktop::View::CGroup::remove()` during `CGroup::destroy()`, triggered by
`Config::Actions::toggleGroup()`:

`Config::Actions::toggleGroup()`
→ `Desktop::View::CGroup::destroy()`
→ `Desktop::View::CGroup::remove()`
→ `Layout::CWindowTarget::assignToSpace() <- SIGSEGV`


This looks like the same class of bug reported in #10342 (a window not
getting properly reassigned to the target workspace's CSpace, leaving a
stale reference to a destroyed workspace's space), but triggered by moving
a window INTO a workspace that hosts an existing locked group, rather than
moving a grouped window OUT. The group itself seems to be the one left with
the dangling CSpace reference once a foreign window lands on its workspace
and leaves again.

Full crash report attached below.
[hyprlandCrashReport1313.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32435063/hyprlandCrashReport1313.txt)

Related: #10342

issues.title: Hibernate pre-sleep hook kills keyboard backlight permanently (no post-resume restore)
issues.body:
**What happens:** `/usr/share/omarchy/default/systemd/system-sleep/keyboard-backlight` forces the keyboard backlight to 0 before every hibernate via `brightnessctl` (comment: workaround for an S4 power-off hang on ASUS keyboard controllers). The glob `/sys/class/leds/*kbd_backlight*` matches any `*kbd_backlight*` LED device though, not just ASUS ones — e.g. `tpacpi::kbd_backlight` on a ThinkPad. There is only a `pre` branch, no `post` counterpart. Result: the keyboard backlight stays off permanently after every hibernate resume, and because `systemd-backlight@leds:...service` persists the current (now 0) value on the next real shutdown, it stays off after regular reboots too.

**Expected:** The backlight should be restored to its previous value after resume, or the workaround should be scoped to hardware that actually has the S4 hang (ASUS-specific LED paths) instead of every `*kbd_backlight*` device.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. On a device with `tpacpi::kbd_backlight` (or any non-ASUS `*kbd_backlight*` device), turn the keyboard backlight on.
2. `systemctl hibernate`, then resume.
3. Keyboard backlight is off and stays off, including after a subsequent full reboot.

**System:** Omarchy 4.0.4-1, kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy, ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 12.

**Suggested fix:** Save the pre-hibernate brightness to a state file and restore it in a `post` branch, or scope the zero-out workaround to ASUS-specific LED device names (e.g. `asus::kbd_backlight`) instead of the generic `*kbd_backlight*` glob.

issues.title: $HOME/.local/bin added to $PATH twice (pam_env.conf + omarchy-zsh shell envs)
issues.body:
### Description

`$HOME/.local/bin` appears twice in `$PATH` because it is added by two independent sources, neither of which checks whether the directory is already present:

1. `/etc/security/pam_env.conf` (PAM session setup, shipped by Omarchy):
   ```
   PATH DEFAULT=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:@{HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:@{HOME}/.local/bin
   ```
2. `/usr/share/omarchy-zsh/shell/envs` (shell init, packaged by Omarchy):
   ```sh
   export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.local/bin"
   ```

So the session `$PATH` (visible in the Hyprland compositor environment) already contains `$HOME/.local/bin`, and every interactive zsh/bash session appends it a second time.

This is harmless at lookup time (the second entry is just redundant), but it is noisy for debugging and for tooling that displays or parses `$PATH`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh Omarchy 4.0.4 install, zsh as default shell.
2. Run:
   ```sh
   echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n'
   ```
3. Observe that `$HOME/.local/bin` appears twice.

### Expected behavior

`$HOME/.local/bin` should appear only once. A guard like the one `/etc/profile` already uses would prevent the duplicate:

```sh
case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;;
  *) export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.local/bin" ;;
esac
```

(Alternatively, drop the PAM entry or the shell entry so there is a single source of truth.)

### System details

- Omarchy: 4.0.4-1
- Shell: zsh
- Session: Hyprland
- Debug log: https://logs.omarchy.org/hmCzXk

issues.title: Weather panel stores and sends the chosen location at full geocoder precision
issues.body:
**Omarchy version:** 4.0.4

When a place is picked in the weather panel's location search, `locationCommit()` in `shell/plugins/panels/weather/Model.js` keeps the latitude and longitude exactly as Open-Meteo's geocoding API returns them: five decimal places, about one metre. `persistLocation()` writes them to `~/.local/state/omarchy/settings/weather.json`, and every refresh then sends them unchanged to two third parties:

- wttr.in, through `wttrLocationQuery()`, which uses the raw `lat,lon` as the path
- api.open-meteo.com, through `refreshDailyForecast()` in `Panel.qml`

A forecast does not need that precision, and it defeats a VPN, because the location is carried inside the request rather than inferred from the IP address. For a named place the geocoder returns a central point, so today the leak is limited to the town. But the stored format accepts any coordinates and `omarchy-weather-location` takes them from the command line, so a precise point entered there is sent as it is.

**Suggested fix:** round to two decimal places (about 1 km) in `locationCommit()` and in `omarchy-weather-location` before storing, and round again when building the two request URLs so existing settings files are covered too. Optionally send wttr.in only the place name.

Related but separate: #9706 and #12127 are about the label shown, not the precision sent.
